quote: Great thanks, please send an invite
action: The deal answer has not changed - on 19 Oct Beckman wrote "Great basis but we're not huge fans of Pasadena," the sixth reader to stop at the submarket and the only one to name the place out loud. What changed today is that Zamir did not accept the pass as the end of it: he asked for a catch-up call anyway, she offered windows, and they booked Tuesday 3 Nov at 4pm ET with Gill, Sacks and Caplan copied. She is waiting on the invite - that is the one thing outstanding on this row. Treat it as a relationship call, not a revival of Allen Genoa; nothing she said suggests Pasadena has become acceptable. The value is that Palatine passed on Canyon Woods purely on California and on this one purely on the submarket, so the firm has now twice declined on geography while liking the basis - worth learning on the call which Texas submarkets do clear their bar before the next deal goes out.

title: Managing Director, Strategic Advisory & Capital Markets
quote: I wish been on road last 4 weeks and not getting much appetite for this profile
action: Zamir asked him this morning for groups that might have interest. The answer is a market read, not a decline as principal - Chase is a C&W capital markets MD, not an LP, and he has been on the road four weeks. 'Not getting much appetite for this profile' is the second independent broker corroboration after Marc Belsky that the blocker sits in the market rather than in the underwriting, and it is the broader of the two: Belsky framed it as Houston, Chase frames it as the profile itself - a stabilized 2023 build at a 6 cap. Tagged profile-appetite rather than houston-sentiment so the Houston count on this page stays honest. The 12 Oct seller and debt-balance questions were answered the same hour and breakfast is still on for 22 Oct, so the relationship is intact; he is simply not a source of equity here. Worth pressing at breakfast on what profile IS getting appetite right now.

quote: It's a good looking property and great basis. We are slowing on our RE investing right now while we watch cap rates reset with the recent rate moves.
action: A current ZMR investor, and the fourth firm to praise the basis on the way to no. Nothing about this deal is the problem - they are standing down on real estate generally until rates settle. Keep warm.

quote: Unfortunately too small for us (would need $25mm+ check to look) but appreciate you sharing.
action: The first objection in the other direction - every other size complaint has been that a check was too big. Rules Singerman out of anything at this scale; worth remembering for a portfolio or a larger asset.

title: Associate Director, Acquisitions
quote: Thanks bud. Houston still a challenge for us so going to sit this one out.
action: Market, not deal. Zamir has already proposed a New York catch-up off the back of it.

quote: Not for us. We don't do Houston. Only Austin and Dallas in Texas.
action: A clean geographic rule. Worth recording so Houston deals skip him and DFW/Austin ones reach him first.

title: Managing Partner
quote: Thanks Zamir but this one's not for us.
action: Same six words as Canyon Woods, and again no reason. Two unexplained passes in six weeks - the relationship is worth a call rather than another email.

title: Managing Principal
quote: Negative unfortunately
action: Resolved, and it is a pass. The ambiguity was whether 'negative' meant he had no feedback to give or that the feedback itself was negative; the thread settles it - Zamir's 21 Oct bump asked 'any feedback on your end?' and this is the answer to that question, signed off with a thank you. No reason attached and none likely to come. Worth noting what he asked on 13 Oct before going quiet - 'what's happening with all the people that don't have a pass next to them?' - which is the same momentum question CastleSquare asked on 22 Oct. Two readers have now asked how the book is filling rather than anything about the asset.

title: CIO / Executive Manager
quote: It was great connecting with you last week. We had a meeting this morning and unfortunately, we are going to pass on this opportunity. We have too many partnership concerns internally that we can't get comfortable with at the moment. We want to finalize this potential partnership and then focus on deploying capital. We changed our trip around and now will be in Chicago for some meetings. The team will be back in the states in March... Best of luck on this one, it is a great a deal for you guys, I am sure you will get a partner on board.
action: THE HOTTEST NAME IN THE BOOK IS GONE. STRE carried heat 5 from 6 October, through the debt matrix, a twelve-minute call on 22 October and a positive internal review, and it has now passed on exactly the thing Camilo flagged on 12 October and told us not to worry about: the long-standing Houston operator they have been invested with for over forty years. His words then were 'this does not reflect any hesitation on the opportunity itself', and his words today confirm it - the pass is about their partnership, not about Allen Genoa, and he closed by calling it a great deal. Three things follow. First, the partner-conflict tag was the right read and the lesson is to price it as a real risk rather than a footnote the next time a prospect discloses an incumbent operator in the market; it has now killed the single most advanced conversation in the file. Second, the 11 November trip is off - the principals were flying in to meet their Houston operator and have rerouted to Chicago, so there is no meeting to salvage and no reason to chase this week. Third, this row was one of the five logged as never having had the package, and the package would not have saved it, because nothing in the objection touches the numbers - but four names on that list are still waiting and that lesson does not transfer to them. The relationship is intact and explicitly reopened: the team is back in the States in March and Camilo said he will reach out with dates. Diarise March, send nothing now.  REOPENED 5 Nov 19:29. After STRE's 4 Nov pass - which was a partner-conflict pass, not a deal pass ('too many partnership concerns internally', a 40-year Houston relationship they did not want to cut across) - Zamir went back at 11:43 with the structural answer to exactly that objection: 'what if we were open to partnering 50/50 with your Houston partner?' Padron's reply does two things at once. He asks us to explain - 'Can you explain more about what you envision with this?' - and in the same breath repeats that 'the timing will not work for us right now' and points at March. So the probability is low and the row is back to live only because a direct question is sitting unanswered. Worth answering properly rather than letting it lapse: a 50/50 with their existing Houston operator is the one shape that solves their stated problem, and Padron's own words on the deal were 'it is a great a deal for you guys'.

followup.ask: Camilo asked "Can you explain more about what you envision with this?" on the 50/50-with-their-Houston-partner idea. Answer it, even though the timing answer is already no.

title: Principal
quote: Sounds great. Don't love houston but let's discuss.
action: Closed as a pass on Zamir's read, 5 November - Rami Hakim never wrote a no, so this is a judgement call rather than their word, and it should be read that way. His only line was 'sounds great, don't love houston but let's discuss' on 2 October, and in thirty-three days it never became a discussion. That made it the oldest live row on the board and the clearest example of a conditional yes that nobody converted. If the raise gets tight he is a cheap phone call, because he never actually declined.

title: Partner
quote: Sorry for the delayed confirmation but initial intuition was accurate unfortunately. Best of luck
action: Closed. The chase drafted at 08:30 ET on 22 Oct went out and he answered inside the hour, after seventeen days of silence on a 'quick look' promised 5 Oct. 'Initial intuition was accurate' points back to that first reply, which is where the content is: no appetite for JV acquisitions in Houston, the basis is strong, the units are small. So nothing changed on review - the Houston screen was always going to decide it and the look was a courtesy. Worth noting for the pattern: this is the second firm today, after Pearlmark, where a single follow-up converted indefinite silence into a clean answer within an hour. Silence on this board has consistently meant unread or deprioritised rather than undecided.

title: Associate, Investment Management
quote: The asset quality is there, but this isn't a market or submarket we're long on right now. The demographic profile was the biggest hurdle… median household income within 5 miles is ~$54K… leaves little room to grow rents over the hold. Rates were the other piece. With the 5-year Treasury up since the 9/21 lender quote, the deal starts with negative leverage at $34M. We're more constructive on Texas markets like DFW (northern corridor) and Austin.
action: The most useful pass we got. Two fixable objections: the $54K CoStar 5-mile median vs. the $71.2K on-site median, and negative leverage at the 9/21 quote. Rebut both in the next version of the memo.

title: Principal
quote: Looks like a good deal, but not a fit for us. Ronnie and I, and much of our investor network, were destroyed in Houston this cyle. Would take something very special to get us back in down there. Not totally opposed, but a going in 6%, even w upside, is not the answer for us.
action: Priced out, not disqualified. Would need a 6.5%+ going-in to reopen. Keep for a deeper-basis Houston deal.

title: Vice President
quote: Tapped out on Houston right now (too much exposure).
action: Portfolio constraint, not a view on the deal. Same answer would have come from Kirsh's send. Re-approach with a non-Houston deal.

title: Principal
quote: Unfortunately, this one is not a fit for us as our fund exposure in Houston is maxed out at this time.
action: Fund-level cap. Revisit after their next vintage closes — nothing about this deal moves them.

title: Managing Partner
quote: It was a pass — Houston's a non-starter right now.
action: Flat market veto, no deal-level read. Nothing to rebut.

title: Investments
quote: We had a chance to review the opportunity… it is not a submarket we are currently pursuing or investing in.
action: Submarket-level no after a real review. Southeast Houston is the blocker, not the basis.

title: Principal
quote: Thanks for thinking of us, Andrew — we're not as focused on Houston right now unless it's affordable at Max rents.
action: Mandate mismatch — they want LIHTC/affordable in Houston. Market-rate will never clear here.

title: Principal
quote: Pass.
action: One word, no reason given. Nothing to work with.

title: Managing Director
quote: That is an unbelievable basis for that quality of product. Unfortunately, Midloch is out on Houston unless it is perfectly located in one of the pockets with phenomenal schools and uniquely high demographics.
action: The fifth firm to praise the basis on the way to no, and the clearest statement yet of the pattern: the asset passes, Houston does not. Their rule is a submarket screen, not a city ban - they would look at a Houston deal inside a top-schools pocket. Nothing to rebut here; file the rule and send them the next one that fits it.

title: Partner
quote: We'd like to have a good handle on how these properties have been renovated and where cash has gone before we evaluate additional acquisitions together.
action: Still the only firm on the board whose gate is ZMR itself rather than the deal. Laura's condition on 12 Oct was explicit - a full reconciliation of the renovation reserve on the existing deals 'before we evaluate additional acquisitions together' - and eighteen days on it is still open. Megan's 30 Oct update names the blocker: the property changed management companies, and accounting systems, three separate times, so the history has to be rebuilt across three charts of accounts, and the team is now trying to reach the prior property manager about 4Q20 activity. NinetyNine44 is the worked example Laura gave - a $4.7M reserve drawn to $638K by year-end 2021 and then showing $1.2M at year-end 2022, which is the increase she wants explained. Laura acknowledged the update today, so the relationship is fine and the thread is live; what is not fine is that Allen Genoa cannot move here until this lands, and the DD clock expires 20 November. Worth deciding whether to put more hands on the reconciliation than Megan alone, because this is an existing LP asking where their capital went - it outranks the raise.

followup.ask: Conditional since 13 Oct. Megan emailed 30 Oct, no answer.

title: Vice President
quote: Thanks for reaching out. Looping in Erin Sullivan who covers TX for us.
action: Filed as referred, but read it as forward motion: on Canyon Woods Rich's answer was that the equity fund was fully specified, and this time he routed the deal to Pearlmark's Texas coverage within three hours rather than repeating it. Pearlmark having a dedicated TX person is itself the signal. The next move is Erin Sullivan (esullivan@pearlmark.com) directly, not another email to Rich.

quote: Understood on Concord and market vacancy, but I don't think we can get comfortable with the spread between underwritten rents and Aria, so we'll have to pass. Please keep us posted on the next one!
action: A pass, and the most informative one on the board because he conceded two of his three challenges and died on the third. Kevin answered all of it on 20 Oct: Concord at Allendale is 2002 vintage so not a true comp; submarket vacancy is diluted by older Class B/C stock, the comp average is dragged by Aria at Burke still leasing at ~63%, stabilized comps average 94.9%, the subject is 94.8% today, and RPM underwrites ~94% in Year 1. Niv accepted both - 'Understood on Concord and market vacancy.' What he would not accept is Aria at Bellfort: 1BRs about $1,165 at 650 SF and 2BRs about $1,450 at 930-1,000 SF, against our underwritten rents. Kevin's answer was that per-SF the two are close and Aria is an outlier on finishes and amenities. Niv did not buy it. Three things follow. One: this is a deal objection, not a Houston objection - he passed on the rent underwrite, which makes him one of only a handful on the board quarreling with the economics rather than the market. Two: Aria is the nearest comp and it is now the known soft spot; Island Capital asked for the 90-day lease trade-out report this afternoon and will find the same gap, so have the per-SF bridge and the signed-lease evidence ready before they ask. Three: he is off the co-GP list. Zamir's 12 Oct send explicitly offered co-GP or pref as an alternative and Niv passed on the asset outright, so the earlier read that Mountain Pacific was a structure question rather than a deal question was wrong. He asked to be kept posted on the next one, and he gave up a useful number on the way out: the Katy deal on his desk is new vintage at $150-160K/unit.

quote: We are going to pass on this one. We are pretty bearish on Houston based on our current portfolio and not focused on new deals there.
action: Both halves of the Houston objection in one sentence - existing portfolio exposure and a bearish house view. Their third pass in a row (Sarasota in January, Logan Farms BTR in March), and the first where the reason is the market rather than policy. Stop sending Houston; the relationship is still worth a non-Houston deal. Note the CC earned this: Scott Pearson is out of the country until 20 Oct and Chad answered in his place.

title: Chief Growth Officer
quote: I will run into a great deal of pushback on a fully occupied property at a 6% cap that nets to $135k a door in a $235k market. If we are going in fully occupied at a 6% on mostly new renters, all of the benefit needs to come from raising rents, so my argument needs to be that the prior owner was 1/3 below market. By the numbers themselves, it looks like a nice deal. Let me know your thoughts.
action: A pass, confirmed by Zamir 4 November. LeCates had written the single most precise objection in the file on 13 October: he would face heavy internal pushback on a fully occupied property at a 6% cap netting $135k a door in a $235k market, because going in fully occupied at a 6% on mostly new renters means the entire case rests on raising rents, and his argument would have to be that the prior owner left rent on the table. Nobody answered it in three weeks and the firm has now closed. That objection is the going-in-yield and the demographics argument fused into one sentence, and it is still unanswered for every reader currently in the model - ABR made the same point on its way out, and Manglar priced it at $27.5M. Keep the sentence; the relationship is cold but not hostile.

title: Director, Investments
quote: Though the basis seems good, ultimately the submarket is not one we could get comfortable with. I appreciate the time walking me through the overview of the project, and hope we can connect on the next one.
action: The most expensive loss of the round so far, and the clearest answer yet on what extra GP capital can and cannot buy. Flagship are Houston-based, at One Greenway Plaza; Zamir pitched it as a deal 'in your own backyard' and offered, in writing on 12 Oct, to put up more than the standard 10% on the GP side at whatever co-invest level made it work. Brian took a call on 14 Oct, Kevin sent crime and safety, the debt matrix, resident demographics, the AR report and comps on 15 Oct, and it went to committee on 21 Oct. It still died on the submarket. A local shop with the full file and an open-ended structural sweetener could not get comfortable, which says the GP co-invest lever does not move a submarket objection - and that offer is still sitting unanswered as a precedent, so it is worth deciding whether it stays on the table for the names that are still live. Note also that he never engaged with the Sunnyside point MLG raised; this is a conviction answer, not an analytical one.

title: Senior Analyst
quote: Regarding the addition of bulk cable / wifi, is there a contract for that? Do other assets in the market also charge for this income?
action: Out - confirmed by Zamir 4 November. Escobar's bulk-internet question (is there a contract, do other assets in the market charge for it) never got a written answer, and the firm has now closed the file, so the question dies with it. Worth keeping the question itself though: KCB asked the identical thing on 3 November and Todd Hanson flagged the bulk-internet income line too. Three independent readers on one assumption means the memo needs a market precedent for the ~$70/unit/month, not just the cost. Marc Belsky had already passed on the market on 22 October, so this closes both Belsky rows.

title: Senior Vice President
quote: While the per unit basis looks attractive, the T1 yield on total cost of 5.2% is below our comfort level. There is substantial growth in the year 1 NOI which we would hesitate to underwrite. The five year cash flow does not reach an 8% YOC even with the growth.
action: The most precise pass of the round, and the only one that puts numbers against ours. Two to answer before the Flagship call: she computes a 5.2% T1 yield on total cost where the teaser leads with a ~6% going-in cap, and she says the five-year cash flow never reaches an 8% YoC against our 7.0% untrended. Reconcile the first - cap on purchase price versus yield on all-in cost are different denominators and we should say which we mean - and decide whether 8% is simply a higher bar than this deal clears. She is the fifth reader to land on year-one NOI growth.

quote: This check is too small for us, and we're taking a pause on new investments for the time being. Digesting some recent deals and focused on asset management.
action: Size and timing, not Houston - he never mentions the market. Nothing to rebut; requalify when they are deploying again and only on a materially larger check.

quote: Unfortunately no movement on the JV front and Houston is tough for us in general right now. Let's catch up in the next few weeks to compare notes.
action: The JV position Zamir asked about has not changed, and Houston is a second strike on top of it. But he asked to compare notes in the next few weeks, which is worth taking - Forum sees enough flow to be a useful read on where equity is actually clearing.

quote: Unfortunately we aren't able to do non restricted market rate in TX right now. Most of what we do requires to have some sort of regulatory agreement or subsidy.
action: The affordability framing was the right instinct and still did not clear the mandate: they need an actual regulatory agreement or subsidy, not rents that happen to sit at 25% of median income. A clean structural rule - do not send them unrestricted market rate again.

quote: Would a Co GP structure interest you?
action: Closed from ZMR's side, not theirs. Kohn asked on 13 October whether a co-GP structure would interest us; Zamir's answer on 4 November is that co-GP is not needed yet. So this is a structure mismatch on a live and willing counterparty, which is a different thing from a pass - Benedict never looked at Houston, the basis or the returns and never said no. Two consequences. The row should not sit in the follow-up queue, because there is nothing to send. And Benedict belongs on a short list of groups to go back to if the LP raise does not close and the structure has to change: they volunteered co-GP unprompted, which almost nobody does. Clairmont wants the same thing. Two names, one structure, parked rather than lost.

title: Principal
quote: The basis you secured coming out of the broken process is a compelling story. Where we land, though, is that we'd need to underwrite to an exit cap rate north of 6.50%, and at that level returns fall below our threshold.
action: The cleanest pass on the board and the most useful. The vintage objection that killed Canyon Woods is gone - he says so - and the whole thing now turns on one assumption: he needs north of 6.50% exit against our 6.00%. Slocumb said 6.25% independently. Two unrelated readers landing above our exit is a tighter, more fixable signal than the rent-growth theme, because it is a single number. Worth running the deal at 6.50% and seeing what survives before the Flagship call.

quote: I sent this around and the team wasn't interested, as this is a pretty rough pocket in Houston and not one where we'd look to invest.
action: Houston-based and the bluntest submarket read we have: 'a pretty rough pocket'. His Canyon Woods objection was no CA and no pre-2010, both of which this deal answered, and he still passed - so the vintage and geography fixes worked and the location inside Houston is what stopped it. Pair this with ARCTRUST on the $150-225K home listings nearby: two readers now say the immediate area, not the city, is the problem.

quote: Is there a time next Monday 3 - 5p that works for you?
action: Out - confirmed by Zamir 4 November. This one is worth looking at squarely rather than filing. Gallo asked for a call slot on 22 October ('is there a time next Monday 3 - 5p that works for you?'), the row sat at meeting stage for two weeks on the teaser alone, no package ever went, and no outbound left ZMR in that window. His written objections were exit cap and going-in yield - both answerable, neither answered. It is not possible to say the silence caused the loss, because HIG may have passed on the merits anyway. But it is the clearest case in the file of a heat-5 row cooling while the materials sat, and it is the argument for clearing the no-package queue before working the cold list.

quote: We'd prefer to invest in a stronger market and submarket as the market stats don't look great, so it's hard for us to underwrite the MtM/burnoff plan.
action: The clearest statement of how the two objections connect: weak submarket stats are why he cannot underwrite the mark-to-market and concession burn-off, which is the entire business plan. Everyone else has raised the market and the rent growth as separate points; he says the first disqualifies the second. That is the argument to pre-empt on Wednesday, and the answer is the same evidence - signed-lease trade-outs and Kevin's burn-off report showing 3.7% T12 to 2.6% T3 to 2.4% Y1 as realised rather than projected.

title: Chief Investment Officer, CFA
quote: We generally like/look at Texas, but Houston isn't necessarily top of list. However, I did take a quick look at the model. When I modestly stress the rent growth, return on capex, and add waterfall/asset management fee assumptions the deal returns don't look compelling relative to other opportunities. I didn't even add in other expenses below NOI that hit every deal as an owner.
action: The only reader who opened the model and stressed it, and the most useful pass of the round because Houston is explicitly not his reason - Texas is fine, Houston is just not top of list. His finding is that the 20.3% does not survive modest stress once rent growth and return on capex are haircut and the waterfall and asset management fees are layered in, and he says he did not even add below-NOI owner expenses. That raises a question to answer before today's calls: whether the headline 20.3% is an LP net number or a project-level one. If it is project-level, every sophisticated reader will do what he did. He also answered the standing question about geography - Texas is not on his no list.

quote: Wants co-GP. [Relayed by Zamir on 22 Oct; West Pine's answer came outside email.]
action: Tim asked for a call on 14 Oct, the follow-up apologising for the dropped Thursday slot went out on 22 Oct, and his answer is that West Pine want to come in on the GP side rather than write the LP cheque. Zamir's position, stated the same day, is that ZMR is not entertaining co-GP until the LP is placed. That is now a policy, not a one-off, and it governs every other structural conversation open on this board - Benedict's co-GP question, JSB's 'never a pure LP', Baltisse's (co)GP mandate and Artisan's majority-GP framing all sit behind the same gate. Six firms have now asked to sit on the GP side and none has offered to fill the $11.65M, which is the shape of the round: the deal reads well to people who want to own more of it and badly to people being asked to fund it. Park Tim until the LP is signed, then come back.

followup.ask: Conditional since 23 Oct.

quote: It looks interesting but we've made a pretty big bet in Houston this year (MF and commercial). So before we make another bet there, we are taking a pause there until we can see how those deals are performing.
action: Houston concentration, not a view on the deal - he calls it interesting and is pausing only until his existing Houston book seasons. That makes him a re-approach once those deals report, not a closed door. Another entry in the column that dominates this round: the reason is the city, not the basis, vintage, check size or returns.

quote: 621 Capital - Wants 2022 and newer at 30-40% below replacement cost. Houston is an actionable market. Potentially concerned with the broader area.
action: Still the slowest name on the board. Slocumb followed up again on Monday 26 Oct and reported on the 28th that 621 is simply being slow - no new view, no objection, no decline. Their stated filter (2022 and newer at 30-40% below replacement cost) is the single best fit for this asset anywhere in the four channels, which is why it is worth one more push rather than writing off. Ask Slocumb for a direct introduction instead of another relay; three weeks of silence through an intermediary is where deals go to die.

quote: BIG unlikely to get there due to location concerns.
action: Slocumb closed this one on 28 Oct and the reason is the location, not the business plan he flagged on 15 Oct. That matters more than losing the name: BIG is a Slocumb-channel reader with no ZMR relationship and no sight of the direct channel's feedback, and it lands on the same ground as Island Capital, FCP, Dean Adler's Houston office, Arc Capital, Sabal, Green Pine and Slocumb's own underwriting. Seven independent parties, four channels, one submarket. The micro-location question is now the central objection on this raise, ahead of Houston generally.

quote: Reported via Zamir, 4 Nov: Manglar came back and said they would be at like $27.5M; they need to be at a 9-10% yield on cost.
action: A hard price answer, and the most specific one the raise has produced. Manglar needs a 9-10% yield on cost, which at this asset's NOI puts them at roughly $27.5M - $6.5M below the $34.0M contract, about 19% off. That is not a negotiation, it is a different deal, and it closes the Slocumb channel: Jeremy's group is a pass and he is still working 621 Capital alone. Two things worth carrying forward. First, Manglar is now the third independent reader to put a number on yield on cost after Contrarian (wants ~9%, stress-tests exits at 7.0%) and Zairick's audit, and all three land in the same place: the 7.00% property-basis YoC is the binding constraint on this deal for anyone underwriting to a yield rather than an IRR. Second, Manglar's five diligence items were never sent, so this pass came without them ever seeing the detail - worth knowing it was the headline economics that failed, not the supporting file.

quote: Arc Capital Partners - Will not invest in this Houston pocket. Weak demographics.
action: The bluntest statement of the micro-location objection in the whole round - not Houston, this pocket. Also resolves the duplicate-risk flag that has been open since the list went out: Arc was on both Slocumb's list and ZMR's draft list, and Slocumb reached them first.

quote: Claritas Capital - Can't meet the project timeline. Unlikely to consider new investments until Q1.
action: Timing, not the deal. Worth a re-approach in Q1 if the raise is still open or a later deal needs equity.

quote: Ulysses Capital Management - More focused on Dallas and Austin in the near term.
action: Another geography no, and a notable shape of it: not that Houston is bad, but that Dallas and Austin come first. Texas is fine; Houston is the part that loses.

title: Managing Partner
quote: Zamir - We are a pass here given submarket within Houston. Believe there are challenges in the near term and will pass on the opportunity. Thanks for following up.
action: Closed, seven days after Kevin sent the full package on 15 Oct. The sequence is worth keeping: on Canyon Woods he said 'No interest here' with no reason; this time the 15 Oct follow-up turned him to 'Yes, please send' inside four minutes, he took the three-pager, demographics, concession burn-off and comp set, and went quiet for a week until the 22 Oct chase. So the follow-ups worked twice on the same man and still ended in a pass - but a reasoned one. He names the submarket rather than Houston, and 'challenges in the near term' is the same read Flagship gave forty-five minutes later.

title: Director, Acquisitions & Capital Markets
quote: Short answer is - we simply don't have a home for this one at the moment. It's a better fit for our core-plus SMA from a return perspective; however, the location (demos, school system etc.) leave a bit to be desired for an investment mandate with a longer-term outlook.
action: The deepest reader on this deal has passed, and the reason is the one the board was built around. Peter put ten written questions to Kevin on 15 Oct, took a call on 20 Oct, received the demographics report, concession report, AR report, track record and updated model, and sat on it for two weeks through a voicemail, texts and two chasers. The answer is not about the basis, the vintage, the concessions, the taxes, the flood zone or the bulk internet - every one of those was answered in detail and none of them is cited. He says the RETURNS fit his core-plus SMA; what fails is the location, and he names demographics and the school system. That is the fifth independent reader to land on affordability and household income after Sabal, Green Pine, Slocumb and Island Capital, and it is the first time one of them walked away from a fully-diligenced position over it. Two things follow. First, the demographics report ZMR sent is evidently not answering the question - it is being read and then used as grounds to pass, so it needs rebuilding or it needs to stop going out. Second, Peter named a real fit on his own side: the core-plus SMA works on returns. If a longer-dated mandate is the obstacle, a shorter-hold structure is the conversation, not this deal. Worth a direct call rather than an email - he apologised for going quiet and asked to stay in touch, and he has read this asset more carefully than anyone outside ZMR.

title: President / Managing Director
quote: While we appreciate the merits of the opportunity, we could not get comfortable with the submarket dynamics and the underlying demographic profile, which ultimately makes it difficult for us to achieve conviction within our investment parameters.
action: A team decision, not a one-line brush-off, and the cleanest statement yet of the objection that now dominates the round: submarket and demographics, with the merits of the deal explicitly conceded. Worth keeping warm - he asks for Isidro Garcia and Ronell Firouz on all future submissions because they screen and will give fast feedback, and he wants a drink in late November. Send him the Resident Demographics Report anyway; it is the direct answer to the thing he could not get comfortable with.

quote: Thanks - too small of a check for us, but thanks.
action: A different reason than his Canyon Woods answer, which was the value-add fund and a wider than 5% exit. The follow-up answered both of those, and the reason moved to size. $11.65M is simply below Prospect Ridge's bar, which is structural and will not change on this deal.

title: Senior Associate, Real Estate
quote: After reviewing it, we've decided this one isn't a fit for us. We're being very selective with our multifamily equity investments right now and aren't looking to add exposure in Southeast Houston.
action: Opened by the follow-up at 15:32, closed by 22:21 the same day - he reviewed and answered inside seven hours. The reason is worth more than the pass: Pennybacker is Austin-based and the most Texas-literate reader on the list, and they will not add exposure in Southeast Houston specifically, not Houston broadly. That is the same submarket line MLG, Arc Capital, Lenox West, 621 and ARCTRUST drew, now from a firm that underwrites Texas for a living. Petrini and Beier were both on it, so this is the house view rather than one associate's.

quote: It doesn't seem cheap enough relative to the risk we're seeing in the market.
action: The first reader in the whole round to say the basis is not good enough. Everyone else has praised it on the way to a no about Houston, the pocket, the check size or the fees - this is the one dissent from the thing the pitch rests on. He passed in eleven minutes, then gave the reason only when Zamir asked for colour, which is worth repeating on every other one-line pass.

title: Managing Principal, Chief Investment Officer
quote: Thank you for following up. We are going to pass on this one for now. I do appreciate the look.
action: A courteous no with no reason attached, but 'for now' and 'I do appreciate the look' leave the relationship open - he is worth a different deal rather than more pressure on this one. Ask him for the disqualifier the way Mavik was asked; the one-line passes have given up real colour every time someone pushed.

title: Assistant Vice President
quote: I took a look at this deal, and it will not be a fit for us. The basis and product type is definitely intriguing, but we are not buying in southeast Houston. The household incomes are below our thresholds, and we worry about our proximity to Sunnyside in this pocket.
action: The most specific version of the objection that now dominates the round: he is the first reader to name the actual neighbourhood, Sunnyside, rather than gesturing at 'the pocket' or 'the demographics'. That is worth more than the pass. Everyone else - ARCTRUST, Marble, Arc Capital, 621, BIG Equity, Lenox West - circled the same concern without naming it; now there is something concrete to measure the asset against, and the Resident Demographics Report can be pointed at it directly. He also answered the coverage question the follow-up asked: Lunde took it rather than Terry Wallen, and he concedes the basis and the product.

quote: Thank you for checking back in! Unfortunately, we're still dealing with a full plate, but feel free to check back in at any time.
action: The same answer Scott Brown gave on Canyon Woods in August - a full pipeline, not a view on the deal - which is why the follow-up went to them at all. Two for two on capacity means it is structural for now rather than something this deal can argue with. Will Hensley answered rather than Scott, and the invitation to check back in at any time is worth taking literally on the next one.

quote: Thanks Zamir. Seems like an interesting basis but we're a bit in a holding pattern on new multi opportunities while we wait to see where treasuries shake out.
action: Another reader who likes the basis on the way out - 'interesting basis' is the same concession Lunde at MLG and Cohen at Lenox West made before passing on something else. What is different here is the reason: not Houston, not the submarket, not the pocket, but rates. Machine is waiting on treasuries before committing to any new multifamily, which makes this a timing pass rather than a view on the deal, and the only one in the round framed that way. Worth a note when the rate picture settles or when the agency quote is locked, since a locked loan removes exactly the uncertainty they named.  10 NOV - THE WARM INTRODUCTION WENT TO HER OLD MAILBOX. Voss forwarded the deal at 19:34 to 'Meredith' at mjonker@machineinv.com. That is the same person: Zamir's 12 October send went to mjonker@, the 16 October reply came back from mrodman@ as Meredith Rodman on the same thread, and his 5 November chase went to mrodman@. She was Meredith Jonker on Michael Regan's March thread. One person, a name change, two live addresses, and the roster still carries both. So the only one of Voss's four introductions that reaches a firm already on this board reaches a person who has seen the deal twice and answered once - and it reaches her at the address she no longer replies from. That is not fatal; a peer vouching for the deal is a legitimate second bite and the rate picture she named has had three more weeks to settle. But Zamir should answer it knowing she already passed, not as an introduction to a new name, and he should reply to mrodman@ rather than the address on Voss's forward. Collapse the duplicate on the roster while it is in view - this is the second alias pair found in two days, after Inbox Capital's m@ and markus.kitunen@, and the third address problem of the week counting Affinius's two domains.

quote: That's directionally correct but the precise timing of when we can actually deploy is still a bit up in the air. Let's stay in touch.
action: The 2027-fund angle was the right one to press - he confirms the thesis is 'directionally correct' - but the fund's deployment date is not fixed, so a January close is still ahead of them. Nothing about the deal is in the way here; it is purely a vehicle that is not open yet, which is the cleanest version of the timing pass in this round. Keep him on the list for the next Texas deal in Q1 rather than pushing this one. Worth noting he signs Brent, and his address line reads Brent Fraker - every send so far has opened with Brian.

title: Chief Investment Officer
quote: thanks for thinking of us, deal seems to pencil nicely based on your comments below. Likely not a fit for us given the geography and non-local sponsorship but we will discuss when Carl gets back later this week and get you defeinitive feedback.
action: The 16 Oct follow-up - concessions realized, the comp set, the exit 23-31% below comparable-vintage trades - landed: he says the deal 'seems to pencil nicely.' The two reasons he gives for leaning no are both about who and where, not the numbers: geography, and that ZMR is not a local sponsor. Non-local sponsorship is new - no one else in this round has raised it - and it is the one objection Kevin can answer personally, since Burke is a former colleague of his. Carl is back later this week and Burke committed to definitive feedback, so this is a live committee look, not a pass. Have Kevin reach out directly before Carl's meeting rather than sending more material.

followup.ask: Reviewing since 19 Oct, silent 16 days.

quote: Thank you for the opportunity but the equity on this project is more than we want to commit at this point. We appreciate your willingness to commit more capital on your side but we generally like to own 90% of a project.
action: A clean close, and the inverse of every other size objection on this board. On Canyon Woods Sergio ruled out $30M or even half of it; the 16 Oct follow-up pointed out that $11.65M sits below that half and explicitly offered to carve to any number that worked. He declined to name one, which is what makes this final rather than a negotiation - the ask was open and he did not take it. The reason is structural, not about Houston or the basis: Vey wants to own 90% of a project, so they are looking for deals small enough that their whole check buys control. At $11.65M for the LP, this is simply the wrong size of vehicle for them. No Houston objection, no quarrel with the underwriting - do not re-engage on this deal, but they stay a fit for a smaller one.

quote: We recently allocated all of the remaining equity from our first closing of Fund 5 to a new deal we are putting under contract, so need to have another closing before we commit to a new deal. Expecting Q1 next year. As such, unfortunately the timing does not work for us right now.
action: The second-wave thesis was right and it still did not matter. On Canyon Woods Adam said he would normally be interested but the equity requirement was slightly too large for the value-add fund until he had a few more closes; the 12 Oct send led with exactly that, at a third the check. He does not argue with any of it - no Houston objection, no quarrel with the basis or the business plan. Fund 5's first close is simply spent, committed to a deal they are putting under contract, and the next close is Q1. That is the third timing pass in the round after Machine and Westport, and all three point the same way: the January close is ahead of where this vintage of capital actually is. Worth a diarised note for Q1 rather than any further push on this deal.

quote: He mentioned that and we had someone underwriting. We're pretty focused on npls and more distressed sits on Texas multi right now. Looks like you got a good one, we just want to do more work to earn the same returns :)
action: Relayed by text rather than email - Zamir met Eric Samek at the LA Roundtable, Eric said Matt was reviewing, and Matt answered Zamir's text the same day. The most useful pass on the board, because it inverts the round's headline finding. Brasa are not avoiding Houston or Texas - they are actively underwriting Texas multifamily right now. What they will not do is a clean one. They want NPLs and distressed situations, on the view that they can reach the same returns by doing more work, which is a direct judgement that a 20.3% IRR is not enough compensation for a stabilized 2023 build. That is the second reader after BIG Equity to say the business plan is too thin - nothing to build - and the two of them together are a sharper signal than any single Houston pass: for value-add and opportunistic capital the problem is that this deal is already done. Note they did real work: someone was underwriting it before the answer came. Keep Brasa for a distressed or NPL look, not for this.

title: Associate, Principal Investments
quote: Thank you for sharing this deal with us. Unfortunately, we are not going to get there on this one. We already have heavy exposure in Houston in this fund, so the bar is extremely high for adding another one. We also have some internal concerns around the specific location. Good luck and please keep us in mind for the next one.
action: The deepest diligence on the board ended in a no, and the reason is the same one the board is built around. Island worked this file for nine days across four names on one thread: Lytle routed it 20 Oct, Bickett took it himself 21 Oct and asked for the 90-day trade-out report, an in-place tenant demographic report and the raw rent roll and T-12, Robertson asked the same afternoon for an unprotected copy of the model, and Kevin answered both inside the hour with 4MB and 21MB sends. They went all the way into the model and still passed - and not on the basis, the vintage, the check or the returns, none of which Robertson mentions. He names two things: Houston exposure already heavy in this fund, and an internal concern about the specific location. The first is the headline finding arriving from a reader who cannot be accused of a shallow screen. The second is the fourth independent flag on this submarket after Sabal, Green Pine and Slocumb, and it followed the demographic report Bickett asked for - which means the affordability reconciliation is no longer a diligence item to prepare for the next reader, it is a reason a reader who had everything said no. Zamir's 29 Oct follow-up at the updated 21.5% did not move them; the answer came seven hours later. Treat the close as genuine - 'keep us in mind for the next one' from a firm that read the whole model is worth more than most live rows - and send them the next non-Houston deal first.

title: Director of Acquisitions
quote: While the cash flow is stronger, our IC would also have a hard time feeling comfortable with the uncertainty surrounding the exit. They are fearful of underwriting for sizeable appreciation in Houston as they believe values are likely to continue to trend downward given the increase in REO activity and other distressed sales. As a result, they are using the projected effective rent at the time of sale as more of a driver of value rather than the cap rate. In this case, our IC would push back on expanding the rent multiplier from 7.6x at acquisition to 9.6x at sale. This metric ignores operational improvements elsewhere, but it is something they're putting a great deal of weight into in this environment.
action:
The single most useful exchange on the board, because it is the only controlled test of the re-underwrite. Eastham passed on 23 Oct on exactly one thing - 'a tough sell to our committee due to the deal level cash-on-cash returns... holding firm on their 5% Y1 hurdle... without factoring in any escrows or prepaids' - while conceding the basis outright. Kevin sent the GSE 5-year fixed with buydown on 26 Oct, and Hertig's first words back on 27 Oct are 'the cash flow is stronger'. The new debt did what it was built to do and the original objection is gone. It bought a different and harder no.

Their IC will not underwrite appreciation in Houston at all, citing rising REO and distressed sales, and has stopped valuing the exit off a cap rate entirely: they price it off projected effective rent at sale and will not accept the rent multiple expanding from 7.6x going in to 9.6x out. Hertig concedes the metric 'ignores operational improvements elsewhere' and tells us they are using it anyway.

This reframes the exit problem the page already flagged. We had argued a flat 6.00% exit contradicts a business plan that harvests the loss-to-lease, and proposed running 6.50% before the calls. Eastham reaches the same doubt from a different direction, which means re-cutting the cap rate alone will not answer them - the rent multiple has to stand on its own. 7.6x to 9.6x is a 26% expansion and it sits in the model that ABR, Island Capital and Equity Resource are all inside right now. Pre-empt it before those calls.

Also worth keeping: the original year-one read still stands as a separate finding. JDI put T1 yield on total cost at 5.2% and called it below comfort, and Eastham's 5% hurdle failed on the same line. Two independent readers on year-one cash, now a third objection on the exit, from a firm that likes the basis.

quote: We do agree that this is a very solid basis, however we cannot get too comfortable with this micro location. We have seen similar basis' on similar products in better locations in Houston. We do like Houston and have investments in Houston, and are looking for more. Generally we are a pass on the Pasadena area.
action: THE MOST IMPORTANT PASS ON THIS BOARD, AND IT BREAKS THE HOUSTON THESIS. Artisan held the deepest file of any firm bar Corebridge - raw T12 and rent roll on 29 October, the re-underwritten model and the debt matrix the same morning - and took a week to answer. The answer dismantles the framing the whole page is built on. They like Houston. They own Houston. They are actively looking for more Houston. What they will not do is Pasadena, and they say so in those words: 'generally we are a pass on the Pasadena area'. So the objection was never the market. It is the micro location, and Houston was only ever the shorthand readers reached for. Worse, they attack the one claim the pitch rests on. The entire basis argument is that $134,921 a door is roughly half of comparable-vintage Houston pricing. Artisan's reply is that they have seen 'similar basis' on similar products in better locations in Houston' - an operating buyer with Houston positions saying the discount is not unique and can be had without the submarket risk. That is a different and harder objection than anything recorded so far, and it earns its own tag. If it is true, the basis stops being a reason to accept Pasadena and becomes a reason to ask why this one is cheap. If it is not true, somebody has to produce the trades that disprove it, because ABR, Manglar, Palatine and now Artisan have all arrived at the same place from different directions. Two firms have now named Pasadena out loud - Palatine on 19 October and Artisan tonight. The relationship is warm and explicitly open for the next deal; the lesson is to lead the next one with the location, not the discount.

quote: Thanks Zamir. The deal review is in queue. We are reviewing a lot of distress in Florida at the moment and that is getting priority over other opportunities. Sounds like there's a bit of time here (from my perspective). We need to play out a few higher priority opportunities in our backyard before we dig in here.
action: Nine days silent, then 31 minutes after the follow-up. Not a pass and not a no - a queue position behind Florida distress in their own backyard. Two things make this more useful than it looks. First, the 12 Oct send already told him the check sits inside the $10-30M range he described for Fund V and offered either an LP position off Fund V or balance sheet, or a GP-side partnership, and he did not object to any of it. Second, he read the timeline as relaxed - 'sounds like there's a bit of time here' - which is wrong against a January close and is the one thing worth correcting. Kurt Heinze is on copy. The honest read: real but slow, and the January date is the lever, not the basis.

followup.ask: Reviewing since 22 Oct and ZMR has not written since. Thirteen days both ways.

quote: Hi Zamir, not a fit for us but appreciate you sending it over.
action: Seventeen minutes after the follow-up, and the answer came from Phillips rather than Travis King, who was the addressee - Phillips was only cc'd on the original. No reason given and none asked for. The follow-up did its job: nine days of silence converted into a clean no, which is what the email explicitly invited. Nothing to chase here.

title: Senior Vice President, LaSalle Value Partners US Funds
quote: We're unfortunately a pass on this one - a little skeptical there is meaningful near-term upside in the rents given where they stand relative to the comp set, and we are actively pursuing another opportunity in Houston that screens slightly more favorably than this one in terms of basis, cap rate and total return.
action: Two sends and ten days of silence, then seventeen minutes. A commitment to look tomorrow, which puts a real date on it. Worth holding the history in mind: Matthew Keen at LaSalle passed on Palm Aire in January, and Paskov himself on the Logan Farms BTR in March said 'please do keep us apprised and we will be ready to jump back in at the appropriate time' - so this is a warm relationship that has not yet transacted. Dan Witte is on the thread. LaSalle is also the Skye Oaks lender relationship, which cuts both ways. | 26 Oct 15:46 ET: pass, and the most useful one on the board because it inverts the round's headline. Every other pass has named Houston itself - exposure maxed, sentiment burned, the submarket, Pasadena, climate. Paskov is the opposite: LaSalle is actively pursuing another Houston deal right now and chose it over this one on basis, cap rate and total return. So Houston is not the gate here; relative value against a live alternative is. That matters for how the next 11 RJL names are pitched - the market-level defence this memo keeps reaching for is not what lost this one. The other half of the objection is rent upside: he is 'a little skeptical there is meaningful near-term upside in the rents given where they stand relative to the comp set.' That is the second reader after Sabal to question the rent spread rather than the submarket, and it lands despite the 15 Oct follow-up that gave him realized concession burn (3.7% T12 to 2.6% T3 to 2.4% Y1) and the two nearest comparable-vintage trades at $171,769 and $149,811 a unit. He read that detail and still did not buy the upside. Worth knowing what the competing Houston deal is before the next institutional send - if it is screening better on cap rate, that is the number to answer. He closed warm: 'Look forward to reviewing the next one.'

title: Founder & Managing Partner
quote: A no for us right now...we're just inundated and I'm just doing pref, and maybe one more acquisition if it clears a high bar. I'm not as hot on Houston for acquisition/JV, I'd do pref though
action: A pass on the LP ask that leaves a door open on structure: he says twice that he would do pref. Three separate reasons stack here - capacity ('inundated'), a product-type limit (pref only, with at most one more acquisition at a high bar), and Houston specifically for acquisition or JV. Note the asymmetry: Houston is a problem for him as equity but apparently not as pref, which is a credit position sitting above our equity. We are not raising pref on this deal, so there is nothing to convert today - but he is the second name after Mountain Pacific to answer an LP ask with 'pref instead', and if the stack is ever restructured he has said yes in advance. Worth keeping for the next deal where a pref piece exists.

quote: Going to be tough for us to take a flyer on this one. I would ask for material price discount.
action: The only reply in the round that attacks the price itself. Everyone else who objected on economics went at the exit cap, the going-in yield or the rent underwrite; Garrett says the entry number would have to come down materially before he would look. That is a direct challenge to the load-bearing claim - that $134,921 a door is already half of comparable-vintage Houston pricing - and it came from someone who did not engage with the comp evidence at all ('take a flyer'). Two readings: either the comp set is not landing, or Houston risk is being priced in as a discount demand rather than named. He is a friend of Zamir's, so the useful follow-up is a phone call asking what number he would want and why, not another email. Note the routine's stored prompt still wrongly lists Loci as never-contact; Zamir confirmed that is not the case and authorised this send.

quote: He said he was going to look it over. They're still open to doing deals with us. [Relayed by Zamir from a phone call; recorded 22 Oct, call date not specified.]
action: Out - confirmed by Zamir 5 November. The row had been live on a relayed phone call from 22 October where Libman said he would look it over and that they were still open to doing deals with ZMR. Nothing was ever written down by them, which is why it sat at reviewing for two weeks on no evidence. The relationship line in that call is the part worth keeping - they are open to ZMR, just not to this.

title: Director
quote: Zamir, they passed. Thanks for the look.
action: Her group passed. Four words, and the heat-5 conditional row that had been open since 22 October is closed. Read the sequence before filing it: Alanna had one equity group in mind, one she had closed with before and described as VERY selective; she asked on 28 October whether there was more room on the price, Zamir answered 'we can try', and no number ever followed. Then nothing for a week until his 4 November chase produced this. It is not possible to say the missing price answer lost it - a selective group that passes in a week was probably never close - but the price question is the one item on the follow-up board that sat unanswered longest while a named buyer waited on it, and it is now moot. Two things survive: she asked on 22 October who else had seen the deal and was never told, which is the same question Ackman-Ziff asked and the same unsent no-fly list answers both; and she is a Director at an intermediary who went to the trouble of working a name for this. Worth a thank-you and a request for the group's actual reason, because a VERY selective buyer's no is worth more than most.

title: SVP, Real Estate
quote: Hey bud thanks for following up can we catch up Friday between 2-5?? Hoping there's some recent trades / live deals we can point to.
action: Not an Allen Genoa conversation - confirmed by Zamir 5 November, and moved off the live pipeline so it stops reading as a stalled deal row. Ace Patel's 13 October note asked to catch up Friday between 2 and 5 and said he was hoping for recent trades or live deals to point to, which is relationship traffic rather than a response to this offering. Keeping the row because the ask itself is useful: he wants evidence of transactions, which is the thing ZMR can supply whenever the next deal goes out.

title: Vice President
quote: Zamir - thanks for following up. We're still working on getting some additional capital in the fund so right now we're going to be a pass on new opportunities, but appreciate you sending this.
action: Closes the loop Rich Dougherty opened on 13 Oct when he routed the deal to Pearlmark's Texas coverage. Erin had the deal for nine days and said nothing; Zamir's follow-up went at 09:53 ET on 22 Oct and she answered at 10:49, inside an hour. The reason matters more than the pass: it is the same answer Rich gave on Canyon Woods six weeks ago - the equity fund is not funded, not that the deal is wrong. Pearlmark has now given a capital answer twice running and nothing about the asset either time, so the file is closed on this raise but the firm is a clean re-approach once that fund closes. Worth asking Erin directly when she expects dry powder, since the 12 Oct email put that question to Rich and it was never answered.

title: Managing Principal
quote: Much better thank you ... Thanks that would be great. | 10 Nov: "Zamir - was out of the country last week. We followed up with all the groups who said they were digging in. In the next 2 days, we'll know if we should throw in the towel here."
action: Engagement letter received 22 Oct 18:00 ET with a 34-name carveout schedule. Cross-referenced against this board: 14 of the 34 have already had the package direct from ZMR - Arc Capital, Atlantic Creek, BIG Equity, Blue Vista, Brasa, Eagle Realty, Eastham, JDI, Marble, Midloch, Nelnet, Pennybacker, SilverCap and Tramview. Eleven of those have already passed, Nelnet is sent-and-silent, BIG Equity sits with Slocumb, and Eastham is live and reviewing as of 21 Oct. A further 9 are firms ZMR already has named contacts for but has not sent to: CIM (Lars Lopatka), Corebridge (on the equity list, and Zamir emailed James Black on 22 Oct), Dome Equities (Daniel Bourla), Equity Resource (Paul Coelho), Hamilton Lane (Mario Giannini), Humphreys (Todd Glass), KCB (Peter Knell), Peak Rock (Brooks Hallock) and Cohen & Steers (J. Rhoden, a live email relationship since May 2025, last touched Feb 2026). That leaves 11 genuinely new names: Abod, Aureon/Quilvest, Calibogue, Corten, JW Capital, Lakerock, Monocle, NCA Realty, ReCap-RGA, Triangle Capital and Vikingprt. So 23 of 34 are already ZMR's in some form and the incremental reach is 11. The terms need legal review before any 'confirmed' reply. 2% on $11.65M is roughly $233K. The non-circumvention clause bars ZMR from contacting any listed group without RJL's prior written consent during the carveout, and bars re-engaging forever with any group RJL introduces if the deal does not close. The non-disclosure clause has ZMR agreeing not to use the list to build relationships independently - which would cover the nine firms ZMR already has contacts for. The fee also attaches to 'any other group that RJL may introduce', which is open-ended, and the tail is undefined. Striking the 14 handles the fee on names already burned but does not by itself fix the circumvention language. | 22:01 ET: second diligence ask - 'besides for replacement cost analysis, could you also provide color on the submarket, crime etc?'. Both answerable from material that already exists: Kevin sent Flagship a Crime & Safety Overview and a Resident Demographics Report on 15 Oct, and those are the two documents this question asks for. Worth noting the irony - Flagship read exactly that package and still passed on the submarket, as did Grandview, and MLG named Sunnyside. Sending the same file to Jonathan without a written answer to the Sunnyside and household-income point repeats the Flagship outcome at one remove. The replacement cost analysis is the genuinely new piece and does not exist yet. Nothing should go out while the engagement terms are unresolved, since the non-circumvention clause is unsigned and the list has already been received. | Response history checked on the 9 names ZMR already has contacts for, inbound versus outbound in Gmail. Four answer directly: CIM Group (Lars Lopatka, 34 inbound, last Aug 2026), Corebridge (31 inbound, Royce Hadden Aug 2026, and Zamir mailed James Black on 22 Oct), Dome Equities (Daniel Bourla, Jul 2026) and Peak Rock (Tujios, Dellinger and Moran all replied Feb 2026). Three have gone cold: Cohen & Steers answered through May 2025 but ignored Zamir's Feb 2026 note, Humphreys has said nothing since Sep 2024, and Equity Resource last produced a postmaster bounce in Jul 2026. One never answers at all - KCB, where Peter Knell at kcbm.com has had 10 emails and returned zero replies ever; kcb-partners.com is a different outfit with an acquisitions@ alias and should not be read as engagement. And Hamilton Lane has zero traffic in either direction: Mario Giannini is a name on the equity list, not a relationship. That sharpens the fee question. Paying 2% for an introduction to CIM, Corebridge, Dome or Peak Rock buys access ZMR already has and uses. Hamilton Lane and KCB are the only two of the nine where RJL could plausibly open a door ZMR cannot, and the three cold names are worth one direct email before conceding them to a carveout. | 23 Oct 14:02 ET: chased the engagement letter - 'Following up to make sure this is not in spam.' No change to any term. Twenty hours after sending it he is already checking, so the silence is now a visible choice rather than an oversight, and the 30-day carveout clock only starts on a 'confirmed' reply. Nothing is lost by taking the weekend over it: ZMR holds the list already and none of the restrictions bind until the reply goes back. | 23 Oct 14:32 ET: Zamir answered the chase with a single word - 'Received'. That is an acknowledgement, not the 'confirmed' the letter asks for, so nothing is signed, the 30-day carveout has not started and none of the non-disclosure or non-circumvention language binds. The engagement is live as a proposal only. Still outstanding on ZMR's side: the replacement cost analysis, submarket and crime colour, and a decision on whether to narrow the carveout to the 11 names RJL could actually open. | 23 Oct 16:54 ET: Kevin answered all three diligence asks - a Replacement Cost Analysis PDF dated Oct-2026 (which did not exist when Jonathan asked for it two days ago), the 15 Oct Crime & Safety Overview, and a written submarket brief covering Port Houston and Project 11, the Ship Channel petrochemical employers, Bayport, Hobby's $470M concourse expansion, the empty 3-mile pipeline and the stalled 81-unit project. Two things to watch. First, the brief states an average resident household income of ~$86.6K. The teaser carries a $71.2K area median, and Slocumb's objection was that CoStar's 1-mile AMIs sit below even that. The two figures measure different things - one the property's residents, the other the surrounding area - but a reader who conflates them sees the affordability number rising under pressure, and this is the single objection that has killed more of this round than any other. Worth stating which is which explicitly before it reaches 34 new firms. Second, the materials went out while the engagement is acknowledged but unsigned, which is the right order - Jonathan cannot work without them and nothing in the package is the carveout list. | 26 Oct 12:36-14:50 ET: the engagement is now agreed, and on ZMR's terms rather than RJL's. Zamir went back with the carveout narrowed to the 11 genuinely new names - Abod, Aureon/Quilvest, Calibogue, Corten, JW Capital, Lakerock, Monocle, NCA Realty, ReCap-RGA, Triangle Capital and Vikingprt - framed as 'the groups we don't know and haven't received the package'. Jonathan took it without argument: 'Ok. All other terms look good? Could you confirm it with these groups?' Zamir confirmed in writing at 14:45 - 'confirmed you are OK to send to the 11 groups i mentioned below and the terms do not apply to the groups i carved out' - and Jonathan closed it with 'Nice.' So the 23 names ZMR already holds are out of the fee and out of the non-circumvention language, and the 30-day clock now runs on 11 names only. That is the outcome the earlier analysis argued for: no 2% on CIM, Corebridge, Dome or Peak Rock, who answer ZMR directly today, and no forever-bar on the three cold names worth one more direct email. What is still undefined is the tail, which the letter left to negotiation and nobody has returned to, and the open-ended 'any other group RJL may introduce' clause - both now matter less with the list cut to 11 but neither has been papered. The household income labelling is still unresolved and these 11 are exactly who will read it next. | 26 Oct 16:49 ET, ninety minutes after confirming terms, Jonathan is already working the file: 'could you send me the updated model in light of the downward movement in treasuries? I think you sent this model at the peak.' Kevin sent the latest version at 17:07, a nineteen-minute turnaround. The point is a good one and cuts in ZMR's favour. The $23.8M agency quote was underwritten at 6.69% inclusive of a 50 bps cushion layered on top of a 5-Year Treasury + 135 bps spread quoted on 21 Sep; if the 5-year has richened since, the rate-lock cushion is now wider than it needs to be and the levered return improves off a lower coupon. Note also what this says about the engagement: he confirmed terms and immediately asked for working material, which is a broker preparing to go out, not one sitting on a signed letter. | 26 Oct 17:07-17:15 ET: Kevin sent the re-run model, Jonathan came back 'Much better thank you' - so the treasury move does improve the numbers, as he suspected. Then Chip caught the thing that matters: 'We should probably add a 2% equity broker fee into this model, as there isn't currently one.' Jonathan agreed immediately - 'Thanks that would be great' - and Kevin re-sent at 17:15. That is worth marking. Every number quoted in this round so far - the 20.3% IRR, 2.25x, 9.9% stabilized cash-on-cash - was modelled without any equity brokerage fee, because until today there was no broker. RJL's 2% on $11.65M is roughly $233K coming out of the deal, and it lands on the equity, not the purchase price. The headline return the 11 new groups will see is therefore lower than the one on every page sent to the 83 contacts before them, and the two sets of numbers are now circulating at once. Chip raising it unprompted, and the broker agreeing to have his own fee modelled against him, is the right way round - but the three-pager and the teaser still carry the pre-fee figures and should be reconciled before they go out again.
