title: Acquisitions
quote: Please send the model, modeled on a 10 year hold horizon. I don't think we'd want to put a refi on this as the value add is not substantial and not worth the interest rate risk... Per the OM the bulk internet charges drive the growth in income. Are other properties in the neighborhood charging for internet?... How many of your rent comps are charging for bulk internet?... 6% exit cap sounds tight despite it being new construction - we don't want to assume negative leverage and Houston is an oil-dependent/notoriously cyclical market... I can also have a call next week Tuesday. | 10 Nov: "I underwrote the deal in detail and made the following adjustments: Reduced occupancy to 93% per Costar average. Increased R&M to $750/units. With the changes above, the return is not meeting our 15% net IRR threshold over 10 years. We have a property struggling with vacancy in Texas right now so our IC will be critical of any lease up assumptions in the state. Happy to review other opportunities that you think could be a better fit for us."
action: THE BEST NEW CONVERSATION ON THE BOARD, AND IT CAME FROM MIKE REGAN'S FIRST DAY OF SENDS. He mailed Megan Gutnikov at 15:07 PT on his own IMN relationship from his CIM days; she answered in 38 minutes, handed it to acquisitions and asked for the model in Excel plus an effective rent study; Chandler Davis read the OM the same night and came back at 01:32 UTC with three specific underwriting questions and an offer of a call Tuesday on his own booking link. Cold to engaged acquisitions reader in ten hours. KCB was one of the four names Zamir struck from RJL's carveout as a known relationship, which until tonight meant nothing because Peter Knell at kcbm.com had never answered a ZMR email in ten tries - kcb-partners.com and a warm introducer were the unlock, not the list. FOUR THINGS TO DO AND ONE TO DECIDE. One, book the Tuesday slot through his link tonight before the week fills; he invited us to forward the invite, so Kevin and Mike both go. Two, the 10-year model does not exist - every version of this deal is a five-year hold with the agency loan's 5-year term as the spine, and he has explicitly said he does not want a refi and prefers 7-10 year debt to match his hold. That is not a tweak to the output; it is a different capital structure, and it needs Kevin to decide whether we quote the 10-year agency option before Tuesday or go into the call with the 5-year and the reasoning. Three, the bulk-internet question is the sharpest challenge anyone has put to this model and it is the FIRST time a reader has attacked the ancillary income rather than the rents: roughly $70/unit/month of income on about $30 of cost is a visible line in the growth, and he wants to know how many of our rent comps already charge for it, from direct experience of having to roll back a RUBS program after tenant blowback. We have never answered that question because nobody has asked it. Note it also collides with the unread Comcast Service Agreement dated August 2026 that Zach Oseland asked seller's counsel for on 7 Oct and never received - if that contract already commits the bulk-internet rights, the upside is not ours to add and this reader will find it. Four, his exit-cap and negative-leverage point is the standard objection and we have the answer. THE DECIDE: he reads Houston as oil-dependent and cyclical, which is the fifth independent reader on the submarket - and Todd Hanson's refinery and jobs data is the honest answer to it, not the Port Houston brief. Go into Tuesday with that in hand rather than around it.  UPDATE 4 Nov: the materials went. Kevin sent 'ZMR / KCB Introduction & Houston Investment Opportunity' to acquisitions@kcb-partners.com with Mike Regan, Chip and Zamir copied - which also routes around the block on zamir@. The four written questions in their 3 November note (ten-year hold with no refi, the bulk-internet precedent, negative leverage, exit cap) are now live with the model in front of them. Nothing owed until they come back.  10 NOV 00:17 - THEY PASSED, AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE NO ON THE BOARD. Nobody else has done this: Pan at the KCB acquisitions desk opened the 10-year model, re-underwrote it line by line, and named the two assumptions that broke it. Reduced occupancy to 93% per the CoStar average. Increased R&M to $750 per unit. On those two changes the deal stops clearing a 15% net IRR over ten years. That is not sentiment, not mandate and not Houston - it is two numbers, and they are both ours. THE OCCUPANCY POINT IS NOW CORROBORATED FROM OUTSIDE AND FROM INSIDE ON THE SAME DAY. The teaser 170-odd firms hold says 'two straight years at ~95% occupancy'. An independent underwriter pulling CoStar landed on 93%. And hours earlier Kevin had already softened that exact line in the Engle send, to 'held occupancy in the low-to-mid 90s, peaking at 95-96% each spring and summer'. Two independent corrections, in the same direction, roughly two points apart from the marketed figure. The 95% claim should not go out again in its current form. The R&M number deserves the same treatment. KCB had to raise it to $750/unit, so whatever is in the model sits below that on a 2023-build - defensible on a new asset, but it is now a flagged assumption from a reader who did the work, and it compounds with the occupancy cut. Note what did NOT break the deal. Chandler Davis's 2 November objections were bulk internet, the 6% exit cap and Houston's oil cyclicality. Kevin's 4 November answer on bulk internet was the best piece of work this campaign has produced - three rent comps already charging ($60 at Hawthorne at Crenshaw, $75 at Dakota at Deer Park, $85 at Advenir at Boulder Creek), the property already wired by Infinity, ~80% of residents already paying for internet individually so the program replaces a bill rather than adding one, installation free and 15 minutes a unit. That answer held. It is the one objection on this board that has been properly closed, and it should be lifted into the memo verbatim for Belsky, Hanson and anyone else who asks. The last sentence is firm-specific and worth filing: 'We have a property struggling with vacancy in Texas right now so our IC will be critical of any lease up assumptions in the state.' That is not the Houston sentiment pattern - it is a live wound in their own portfolio, which no re-cut of this deal reaches. They asked to see other opportunities, so the relationship Mike Regan opened survives the pass.

followup.ask: Passed on the re-underwrite. No reply needed on this deal; they asked to see others. Fix the 95% occupancy claim and check the R&M line before the next send.

quote: While reviewing the model, I noticed a few things that looked like potential errors... To achieve 7.10%, roughly $2 million of required capital was excluded from the denominator... The Sources table clearly states the Total Equity required is $13.07M ($11.76M LP + $1.30M GP). The calculated 'Levered - Project Level' returns (and the 5.9% Year-1 Cash-on-Cash) use $12.73M as the denominator instead of $13.07M. $340K was subtracted, which artificially boosts the reported Cash-on-Cash and IRR... Returning $6.37M total on a $1.3M investment is mathematically a 4.88x multiple. | 4 Nov: "Thanks for the detailed clarifications and the updated model. That makes sense. I'll review the updated figures and let you know if I have further questions."
action: THE SECOND INDEPENDENT READER TO FIND THE SAME ERROR, AND HE BROUGHT THE RECEIPTS. Todd Hanson flagged on 2 Nov that the IRR and CoC looked like they were computing off $12.7M rather than the full $13.1M. Zairick has now opened the model and named the exact figure: $12.73M used where the Sources table says $13.07M, a $340K understatement of the denominator that flatters both the cash-on-cash and the IRR. Two readers, working independently, one of them with the model open. This is no longer a suspicion to check - it is a confirmed defect, and the number it inflates is in front of roughly 180 groups. HE ALSO FOUND TWO MORE, AND THE FIRST IS BIGGER. The headline 7.10% untrended yield-on-cost is measured against purchase price plus acquisition fee plus capex, not against the $36.87M of total capitalization the LP actually funds on day one. Put the $760K of loan closing costs, the $476K rate buydown, the $691K of tax and insurance escrows and the $252K operating reserve back into the denominator and the true yield on total cost is 6.70%, not 7.10%. That is 40 basis points on the single metric this deal is being sold on, and it sits directly on top of the going-in cap of ~6% that half the market has already pushed back on. Third, the OM claims a 6.24x GP equity multiple where $6.37M returned on $1.307M invested is 4.88x. Less consequential to an LP, but it is a third arithmetic error in the same document and it is the one a careful reader cites when deciding whether to trust any of the others. WHAT TO DO. Kevin has to take all three tonight, not just the equity base: confirm or correct, and decide what the corrected set actually is before another email goes out. Then the four groups who are live and have the model - KCB, Artisan, Eastham, Island Capital - need the corrected numbers from us before they find this themselves, because a reader who discovers a 40bp overstatement on their own does not come back. HIS OWN THREE QUESTIONS ARE EASY AND SHOULD NOT WAIT ON THE REST: minimum and maximum LP ticket, distribution frequency, and whether the hold is five years. Answer those in a short reply tonight and tell him the model points are being checked and he will have an answer tomorrow - he has earned a straight response. Note what he is: a YPO member writing from a personal gmail who read the OM and the model line by line within eighteen hours of receiving them. That is the most rigorous read anyone has given this deal, and it came from individual money, not an institution. | RESOLVED, AND THE MODEL HAS BEEN RE-RUN. Zamir answered in full at 16:46 PT and attached an updated model reflecting the tax consultant's report and current Treasury rates; Zairick came back four hours later with 'that makes sense' and is now reviewing the new figures. He is the only reader who has audited the model line by line and then accepted the answer, which makes him the best validation the numbers have. THREE THINGS CAME OUT OF THE EXCHANGE AND ALL OF THEM CHANGE WHAT GOES IN FRONT OF EVERYONE ELSE. One, the yield-on-cost methodology is defended rather than conceded: ZMR measures it unlevered at property level on $34.83M of purchase price, buyer closing costs and capital plan, excluding financing and structure items, which is the conventional treatment and is comparable to market cap rates. Zairick had assumed the acquisition fee was in the denominator; it is not. On full capitalisation the figure is 6.70%, and both numbers are now footnoted in the presentation. Two, the $340K is confirmed as deliberate, not an error: 21.5% / 2.33x are DEAL-LEVEL returns before the acquisition fee and the 1% asset management fee. Three, and this is the one that matters most, the LP number was disclosed for the first time: net of all fees and promote the LP gets 17.5% / 2.01x on its $11.77M, and on the updated model 17.1% / 1.97x. Every email in this campaign has led with the deal-level figure. THE UPDATED SET, which supersedes everything: 20.9% IRR / 2.27x deal level on $12.69M; LP net 17.1% / 1.97x on $11.73M; total equity $13.03M; 19.8% / 2.19x on total equity net of fees; YoC 7.00% property basis and 6.62% on $36.83M; GP multiple 4.65x. He also got the three structural answers nobody else has been given: minimum cheque $1M with flexibility for people Zamir knows, quarterly distributions, five-year hold.

followup.ask: He found specific model errors - the $2M excluded from the YoC denominator and the $13.07M equity line. Needs an answer from Kevin, not a thank-you.

action: A clean double pass off the Monday follow-up, and the second reason is the useful one. Zamir mailed Robin Potts with Schlee and Baccile copied on 30 Oct; Schlee answered for the firm. It is the most consistent single finding in the round and it argues for a check-size floor on the institutional lists and, on the family-office side, for stating a minimum ticket so the opposite problem does not bite. Nothing to work here; Canyon is a name for a larger deal.

title: Director, Acquisitions

That is a finer distinction than it looks and it is the fourth time it has come back in those words: Virtus knows Texas, sits two hundred miles away, and still will not go to this part of Southeast Houston. When the objection is Houston-the-city it can be argued with basis; when it is the submarket specifically, from a reader who underwrites Texas for a living, the only answers are the demographic and employment facts - and those are exactly what Todd Hanson put a question mark over on 2 Nov with the zip 77017 population and jobs data. title: Managing Director, Real Estate
quote: We are operating under the belief of higher rates for longer and are trying to create deals like this with YOC closer to 9% and stress testing exits at 7.0%. Considering that the untended YOC is 7.10%, this does not seem like it is a deal for us at this time. Good luck with this opportunity. the basis looks to be attractive.
action: THE MOST EXPENSIVE PASS OF THE ROUND, BECAUSE THE NUMBER HE PASSED ON IS WRONG. Halperin did the work - Gil Tenzer handed him the deal and he came back with a clean, quantified bar: he wants roughly 9% yield-on-cost and stress-tests exits at 7.0%, and 7.10% untrended YoC does not clear it. Now put that next to what Daniel Zairick found this morning. The 7.10% is measured against purchase price plus acquisition fee plus capex, not the $36.87M of total capitalisation the LP actually funds, and the true yield on total cost is 6.70%. So Contrarian declined on a figure that is 40 basis points better than the real one. Two consequences. First, this is hard evidence that the YoC overstatement is not academic - it is the exact metric a serious reader screens on, and the first thing one of them did was measure it against a hurdle. Second, nothing here is recoverable by re-presenting: at a true 6.70% against a 9% target the gap is not 40bp, it is 230. Do not go back to Contrarian on this asset. Do note that he praised the basis on the way out, which is now the twenty-somethingth reader to do so, and that the reply came from a Managing Director who was cc'd in rather than from Dacker Chen, who was the addressee.

quote: Thank you for sharing this opportunity. We would be interested in learning more about the investment. Please feel free to send over the full package so we can review the opportunity in greater detail.
action: THE FIRST CONVERSION OFF THE SFO WAVE, and it arrived under two hours. Zamir mailed Willian Bueno at 16:07 with Tiago Kretzmann and Frederico Becker copied; Becker answered for the firm and put Willian and Marcelo Sanvitto on the reply, so four people at a Brazilian family office are now on the thread. No objection of any kind - not Houston, not the submarket, not size. Send the package, but send the CORRECTED one: they were pitched the 21.1% / Year-1 11% set, and both the equity base and the yield-on-cost in that set are now known to be wrong. A first-contact family office that reads a package and finds three arithmetic errors does not come back, and this is the only thing the SFO list has produced so far. Worth pairing the package with the minimum-cheque answer up front, since a single family office rarely writes $11.77M.

followup.ask: Kevin sent the full package 3 Nov, 49 minutes after the ask. Their move.

quote: Thanks for reaching out. This is not our space.
action: Not an investor at all - Smartbox.ai is a UK artificial-intelligence software company trading as Gravicus, and their mail server tagged the email as external to Gravicus. This is list contamination, not a pass, and it is the clearest single piece of evidence that the FinTrx-sourced SFO list has not been screened for whether the firm invests in anything. He answered politely within two minutes, which is more courtesy than the send deserved. Remove the domain and, more to the point, screen the remaining names on the list for whether they are investment firms before the rest goes out.

title: Vice President
quote: Unfortunately, this is not a fit for us as real estate is out of our core scope, but appreciate you thinking of us here. Look forward to connecting on the next one.
action: The Carlson family office does not invest in real estate at all - it is out of their core scope, full stop. Not a pass on Houston or on this deal, a firm that was never a candidate. Third name off the Rest-of-SFO list today that should not have been on it. Borg was a cc, not the addressee, and answered for the firm within ninety minutes; he left the door open for other asset classes, which is worth nothing for a multifamily raise. Remove the domain from the SFO list.  9 NOV 17:58 - HE SENT THE SAME PASS AGAIN, AND THE REASON WHY IS THE FINDING. Borg re-sent his reply word for word, prefaced with 'I'd responded last week but apologies if it didn't go through.' It did go through. His 3 November pass arrived, was read and has been on this board for six days. What did not happen is the only thing that should have followed: he was chased anyway, at 05:53 this morning, as though he had never answered. So this is not a deliverability problem - it is the suppression list failing in the other direction, and Borg has politely apologised for a lapse that was ours. That makes four known instances of the same fault, and it is the most expensive recurring error in the campaign: Connelly objected on 2 November that 'your AI obviously isn't working very well' after being mailed a second time post-CASL complaint; Affinius escalated on 4 November with two senior partners copied - 'We already passed. Please remove us from the distribution'; Carl-Gerrit Deilmann opened this morning with 'I guess I told you before'; and now Carlson. Three of the four produced irritation and one produced a removal demand. The fix is mechanical, not editorial: before the next chase wave goes out, difference the send list against the 268 recorded replies and against outreach.json's suppressed block. Every firm on this board has already answered, and chasing any of them can only cost goodwill. Borg's own answer is unchanged and final - real estate is outside Carlson's core scope - so nothing here needs a reply beyond not writing to him again.

quote: Thanks for the email and the details of your project. Very strong! We do not invest outside of our own projects at this point. In fact, we are looking for LP equity providers like you for our Marriott extended stay hotel development.
action: THE LIST IS SO UNSCREENED IT IS NOW SOLICITING OTHER SPONSORS. Redfern is not an investor - he is a developer raising LP equity for a Marriott extended-stay hotel, and he answered a capital solicitation by soliciting capital back. He did praise the deal ('Very strong!') before explaining he only invests in his own projects. Fourth name off the Rest-of-SFO list in one afternoon that was never a prospect, after Smartbox.ai (a UK AI software company), Carlson (does not do real estate) and Certina (unsubscribed outright). That is four in roughly a hundred sends, which puts the contamination rate somewhere near four percent before counting the twenty-two addresses that bounced. Remove the domain, and treat this as the argument for screening the remaining names by firm type before any more of this list goes out.

quote: We are not making any external investments currently as we have several internal initiatives that we are focusing on. All the best with your capital raise.
action: Sydney-based, and paused on all external investment while they work internal initiatives. A clean timing pass with no view on Houston, the basis or the size - nothing to argue with and nothing to re-send. Worth one note for the list work: this is the second Australian name on the Rest-of-SFO list after KIN Group told us in blunt terms to remove them, and an Australian recipient is an odd fit for a $11.77M US multifamily LP cheque in any case. Adrian was the cc; Anya Haywood was the addressee.

title: Managing Director
quote: We unfortunately will have to pass at this stage as we do not currently have an allocation to real estate within our investment portfolio. We appreciate you reaching out and would be happy to stay in touch should our investment strategy or allocation priorities evolve in the future.
action: Bahrain family office with no real-estate allocation at all - not a Houston objection, not a pricing objection, simply an asset class they do not hold. Courteous and open to future contact, so no suppression needed, but there is nothing here to re-pitch and no follow-up is warranted on this deal. Worth noting for the list work: the send went to Yousef Al Quraishi with Cem Kutuk and Ayman copied, and it was the cc who answered - the fourth time this week that the reply came from a cc rather than the addressee, which is the single clearest argument for mailing every contact at a firm rather than one. Ayman signs from anfal.com, a related entity, so the alquraishi.com address is live but his working address is elsewhere.

title: Growth Equity
quote: Thank you for sharing this opportunity. It is outside of our scope and hence not for us. Wish you best of luck with the process.
action: The Maersk family holding company, and Jonas sits in Growth Equity out of Singapore - they buy and build operating companies, not 252-unit garden apartments in Southeast Houston. A clean out-of-scope note with no reason to follow up. This one is a list-quality data point rather than a prospect: A.P. Moller Holding is a multi-billion-dollar industrial holding company that appeared on a single-family-office list, which is the same contamination pattern as Smartbox.ai and CGC Properties. It belongs on the screen-out list for any future wave, not on a suppression list.

action: Fully allocated to real estate for now, and explicitly asks to be kept in mind for the next one - a timing pass, not a view on the deal. This came off the third touch: the original 27 Oct send, a 29 Oct follow-up, and Zamir's 2 Nov call request, and it was that third push that produced the answer. Keep the address live for the next deal and do not re-send on Allen Genoa. Gerardo was the co-addressee and is copied.

action: Three words and nothing else - no reason, no counter, no door left open. Charlotte-based, Alexa Calahan copied. There is no objection here to answer and no information to extract, which is its own small data point: a same-day one-line pass from a principal usually means the deal was screened and dismissed on something structural (size, market or asset class) rather than read. Mark it closed and spend no more time on it. Keep the address live - the reply arrived cleanly and Lee is reachable for a future deal.

quote: Thanks for following up, don't see this on as fit for us but appreciate the look.
action: A one-line no from a $80B+ manager with no reason attached, arriving only after Zamir's 2 Nov chaser - the 30 Oct original drew nothing. Clarion runs core and core-plus open-end vehicles; a $11.77M LP cheque into a single 252-unit asset is an order of magnitude below what those funds write, so this is a size and mandate mismatch rather than a view on Houston. The send went to Khalid Rashid with Andrew Palmquist and Robert Wilshusen copied, and it was Brent, a fourth name not on the original To line, who answered - the fifth time this week a cc rather than the addressee has replied. Nothing to re-pitch here.

title: CEO
quote: This looks pretty interesting. It's amazing what is available in market right now. Unfortunately, timing isn't going to line up. We've got a number of assets that we are refinancing/recapping that are sucking our equity at the moment. Keep sending across what you are seeing though.
action: The warmest pass on the board. The CEO of a Calgary firm read it, liked it, volunteered that the basis is remarkable - 'it's amazing what is available in market right now' - and asked to keep receiving deals. The only obstacle is that his own equity is tied up refinancing and recapping existing assets, which is a balance-sheet timing problem and nothing to do with Houston, the submarket or the underwriting. This is exactly the profile worth a named follow-up in the first quarter rather than another blast: he asked to be sent what ZMR is seeing, which is an invitation, and he answered personally within a day of a single chaser. One caveat for the list work - ICM is Canadian, and the Connelly CASL complaint question is still unanswered. John asked to keep hearing from us, so consent is not the issue here, but if the decision is to drop Canada wholesale he should be carved out of it by hand.

quote: Alicia shared the below information with us for review, thank you for providing. If you are able to share the project package and agency loan term sheet, that would be helpful for our review. | 10 Nov 21:55: "We had a chance to review internally and it's not a fit for us. We look to have some level of deed-restricted affordability and mostly look at transit-oriented, urban infill projects."
action: A live materials request, and the best news of the day. The 30 Oct send went to Alicia Glen alone; she has passed it internally to Natalie, Sara Myerson and Marissa Schaffer, and the firm is now reviewing as a team. Alicia Glen is the former New York City Deputy Mayor for Housing and Economic Development and M Squared is her platform - a serious, policy-literate reader, which cuts both ways given that five separate groups have now pushed on the submarket's demographics. Send the package today. One problem to solve first: she has asked for the AGENCY LOAN TERM SHEET, and there isn't one. Kevin told ABR on 19 Oct that W&D will only go out for term sheets once the financing strategy is finalised; what exists is the W&D debt matrix. Send that, label it plainly as indicative pricing rather than a term sheet, and say when a real one is expected - do not let a document gap read as evasion to a first-time reader. Also note the returns in the 30 Oct send are the superseded 21.1%/2.30x set; Zairick's corrections give 20.9%/2.27x deal-level and 17.1%/1.97x LP net, so the package should carry the corrected numbers, not the ones in the email she is replying to.  PASSED, AND THE REASON IS A MANDATE THIS DEAL CANNOT MEET. M Squared needs deed-restricted affordability and prefers transit-oriented urban infill. Allen Genoa is fully market-rate garden product in Southeast Houston, so no re-cut reaches them. NOTE WHAT DID NOT STOP THEM, because it is useful. Natalie Hunter published their whole box on the way out: check size $5-30M in GP, LP OR PREFERRED positions; 5-7 year hold with extensions to ten; minimum 6.5% yield-on-cost and mid-teens returns. Allen Genoa's $12.03M ask sits mid-range, the hold matches, and the 7.00% untrended YoC clears their floor. Size, structure, hold and returns were all fine. Only the affordability test failed. Zamir apologised at 15:02 ET for missing the 3:30 slot, Assiran came straight back with 'Can you talk at 4:30 Et?', an invite went out at 20:53 and he accepted it 37 seconds later. Half an hour, Google Meet (meet.google.com/vca-mfvx-jyk). Kevin and Chip are invited and neither has responded - someone from the team should be on it. A LATE APOLOGY RECOVERED THIS ONE CLEANLY. Assiran offered 3:30 and got nothing; rather than go quiet he re-offered an hour later the same afternoon. That is the second row today recovered by apologising instead of letting it lapse, after Manulife - worth remembering against the five slots this campaign has already let expire in silence. ONE THING FOR THE ROSTER: the invite also carries kassiran@caphealthgroup.com. Assiran runs two domains, and Capital Health Group is the healthcare vehicle - mail the cfg.bank address, not both, or he gets everything twice. Fourth address-hygiene fault this week.  THE CALL HAPPENED, AND IT ENDED IN A HANDOFF RATHER THAN A CHEQUE. Zamir at 21:42: 'Hey Ken, Great chatting. Please connect me with the right people who cover multi for you guys, and go Eagles.' So Assiran is not the buyer - CFG Bank is a Baltimore lender and he is routing to whoever covers multifamily. Warm, friendly, and one step removed from capital. THE HANDOFF IS NOW THE WHOLE VALUE OF THIS ROW AND IT IS UNANSWERED. Until Assiran names someone, there is nothing here. He is well disposed - he re-offered a slot after being stood up once - so a short nudge in a day or two is reasonable, and worth pairing with a note on what ZMR would want from CFG, because a bank that covers multifamily is a debt relationship as much as an equity one. Fifth firm to refer us onward after Cigna, Elmington, Arete and Boyd Watterson.  GEMINI CAPTURED THE CALL, AND IT WAS MOSTLY ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE. Notes landed at 22:52 from the Google Meet - note the contrast with Oaktree, where the Meet failed, the call moved to Zoom and no record survives. Allen Genoa got four lines: 2023 vintage, $134/door against a Houston comparable-vintage average of $230,000/door, an in-place cap rate of 6.2%, 40% below replacement cost, and an $80 per month gain from bulk cable and wi-fi. THE REST OF THE CALL WAS AN OREGON SENIOR-HOUSING PORTFOLIO - three McMinnville buildings, NHI pricing the real estate at $53M and $60M with ancillary value, 75% leverage needing $14M of equity, mezzanine options explored up to 85% to cut that, a $500K NHI deposit possibly releasable as equity, an 8.25% cap supported by state Medicaid programs, and Katherine Burton Gray and Bloomfield Capital named as mezz sources. That is a separate ZMR matter and does not belong to this raise, but it explains what CFG actually is here: a financing relationship, not an LP. ASSIRAN OWES TWO THINGS, not one. He is to connect Zamir with CFG's multifamily group, AND to come back by Friday or Monday with a higher-leverage financing strategy including 100% financing options. Zamir owes a due-diligence list, and Assiran is sending materials over. THREE NUMBERS ON THIS CALL ARE NOT IN ANY MARKETING SET. The in-place cap of 6.2% sits against a going-in cap marketed as 6.00% tax-adjusted; 40% below replacement cost appears in no bullet on any version of the teaser; and bulk internet was described as $80 a month where every written version says ~$70 of income against ~$30 of cost. Small on their own, but this is the same drift that has produced seven number sets, and it is now happening out loud on calls as well as in documents.

quote: Unfortunately, I don't think this one will be a fit for us. Our fund is nearing its full allocation in Houston, so we're being extremely selective on any additional opportunities.
action: The textbook version of the objection this whole board was built around, and worth recording precisely because it is the cleanest statement of it in the file: the fund is nearing full allocation in Houston, so the bar for anything further is extreme. Nothing about the basis, the vintage, the submarket or the returns - they are simply out of room. That is a different failure from Artisan's (wrong submarket) and from Alpaca's (wrong city within Texas), and keeping the three distinct matters: exposure-capped buyers come back when a position sells, submarket objections do not resolve at all for this asset. Two practical notes: send congratulations rather than a chase, because a warm two-line reply now is worth more than anything else available here; and put a January reminder against the name, since he set the date himself and will expect the follow-up. action: A courteous strategic pass from the Pinault family's holding company in Paris. Artémis holds Kering, Christie's and Puma - US garden multifamily was never within a plausible distance of what they do, and the useful conclusion is about the list rather than the deal. The European slice keeps producing polite scope passes from operating holding companies, which is the signature of a universe assembled from a generic family-office database rather than a real-estate screen. Count it alongside A.P. Møller, Excession, KKCG and Gardner Standard.

quote: Mr. Randall appreciates you sending this over and asks you to continue to do so in case one comes up that he might be interested in. He will pass on this one.
action: A pass on this deal paired with an explicit standing request for the next one - relayed by his assistant, which means Randall read it and dictated a reply rather than ignoring it. No reason given, so there is nothing to learn about the asset, but 'continue to do so' is a rare and valuable thing on a cold list: an open invitation from a principal to keep sending. Make sure the roster records that as a positive flag rather than filing the row as a dead pass, because the one risk here is that a suppression sweep treats this like any other no and drops him. He should be on the next deal's first wave.

quote: Thanks for the outreach and the follow up. Looks like an attractive deal, but we don't do real estate transactions. Separately, John Hughes is no longer with the firm.
action: Out of scope - Corinthian is a private equity firm that does not do real estate - but he called the deal attractive on the way out, which is the pattern that recurs through this whole file: readers who cannot buy it still like the look of it. The operational content is the second sentence. John Hughes has left the firm, and Clay volunteered that unprompted, so the roster should retire that address now rather than waiting for a bounce. That is the second departure surfaced today after Eldridge Acre's, both found by replying humans rather than by the bounce log - which is an argument for reading the replies rather than only the mailer-daemon output.

quote: We're an office company.
action: Four words, and they close the file. Spear Street is a San Francisco manager that buys and repositions office - that is the whole firm, not a sleeve of it - so multifamily was never going to land however the numbers read. Worth noting what it cost to learn that: the original 30 October note, a 2 November follow-up ('would love to talk through the deal if it's of interest'), and a third chase this morning at 07:22 asking for a call, before Grassi answered at 11:51 ET. Three touches to a firm whose mandate the list should have screened out. No tag, no nurture, no reason to re-approach on a Houston garden deal - but the reply itself is civil and the name is worth keeping for anything office-adjacent.

quote: Thx Zamir - I asked around and think I'll pass on this. Appreciate the outreach...
action: A pass, but one that was actually shopped internally first - 'I asked around' means Hood put it in front of colleagues before answering, which is more than most of today's noes got. Sonen is a San Francisco impact manager, so a market-rate Houston garden deal with no stated impact thesis was always going to be a stretch for their mandate; he gives no reason, so there is nothing to rebut. Three touches to get here (30 Oct, 2 Nov, and this morning's 07:16 call request) and the reply came back inside twelve hours of the last one. Civil, no friction, worth keeping warm for anything with a workforce-housing or affordability angle - but nothing to chase on Allen Genoa.

quote: NOT INTERESTED
action: Two words in the subject line, nothing in the body, answered about nine hours after a send that went out at 09:47 this morning. Worth noting the mechanics: it came back to zamir@zmrcapitalgo.com, one of the GMass alias domains, which means this is blast traffic rather than a named approach, and the Spanish-language quoting ('El 5/11/2026, a las 9:47 am, Zamir Kazi escribio') confirms a Colombian wealth-management house reading a cold English-language US multifamily pitch. He does not ask to be removed, so this is a pass and not a suppression - but the capitals are a signal. On a list where tone is the only early warning of a complaint, this is the one worth not mailing a third time.

title: Chief Revenue Officer
quote: We do not typically accept LP equity raise requests unless we're involved in the loan guarantee portion.
action: Read this as a decline with a named door rather than interest. Impex is a Houston shop on Westheimer whose business is credit enhancement, and Munshi's first question back was the tell - 'Is Impex needed for a loan guarantee/credit enhancement for the debt?' Zamir answered straight ('No we are looking for common equity on this, is that something you'd guys would do?') and got the mandate line in six minutes. The door is real though: this deal carries a $23.8M agency loan that needs a balance-sheet guarantor for the non-recourse carveouts, and Zamir had already written on 3 Nov that he is flexible - 'straight LP, co-GP, or something in between' - and open to paying a fee. If ZMR wants Impex, the ask is a KP / guarantor role with equity attached, not an LP cheque. The row sits as conditional for exactly that reason and for no other; left alone it is a no. Worth noting this was a warm thread - Zamir reopened an August conversation about Impex's own disposition plans and the Grand at Stone Creek, and that half is still unanswered.

title: Private Markets | Real Estate
quote: Hi Zamir, sorry for the delayed reply. We don't have a capital fit for this at the moment.
action: The largest name on the list answers, and answers short. 'No capital fit at the moment' is the sort of line that means a $11.77M LP cheque is below the size at which BlackRock Private Markets can do anything, rather than anything about Houston or the basis - nothing in the reply touches the deal. The apology for the delay is the only warmth in it, and it came off the third touch (30 Oct, 2 Nov, and this morning's 10:19 call request). Nothing to rebut, nothing to chase, and no reason to read a Houston signal into it. Keep Burns for a fund-scale deal; he is not a prospect for this one.

title: Partner
quote: Thanks for following up. Unfortunately Houston is not a market we're actively targeting at the moment.
action: One more for the column that already explains this raise. Declaration Partners is the Bethesda family office built around David Rubenstein's capital, and Cohen is a partner answering personally with David Rabin copied, so this is the firm's view rather than a screen. The wording is the familiar shape: not the basis, not the vintage, not the $11.77M check, not the returns - the market. 'Not a market we're actively targeting at the moment' is a capital-allocation posture, the same tag Alpaca's reply earned when they said they were doing Dallas instead. Nothing here is answerable with a better deck. Three touches to get it (30 Oct, 2 Nov, and this morning's 10:29 call request) and the answer came back at 18:19 ET, polite and final.

quote: Hi Zamir. Too small and this is not a target submarket of Houston for us. Thanks for sending
action: Twenty words, two objections, and the second one is the interesting half. Apollo passing on size is unremarkable - an $11.77M LP cheque is a rounding error at that balance sheet, and the board already carries the same reason from Northwestern Mutual, who put their JV range at $75-150M. What is worth reading twice is 'not a target submarket of Houston for us'. Kaplan does not say Houston. He says this part of Houston. That is now the fourth independent reader to locate the problem at the micro level rather than the market - Palatine named Pasadena on 19 October, Artisan said on 5 November that they have 'seen similar basis' on similar products in better locations in Houston', and the affordability thread from Sabal, Green Pine, Slocumb and Island Capital is the same objection wearing different clothes. The board's headline is that almost every pass names Houston rather than the deal; this is the refinement of that finding, and it is less comfortable, because a submarket objection cannot be answered by waiting for Houston sentiment to turn. Nothing to chase here - but the pattern belongs in how the Meadowbrook/Allendale story gets told to the live rows.

quote: Hi Zamir, thanks for reaching out and following up. Unfortunately the team is focused on other opportunities at the moment so this is a pass for us. We wish you success on closing the deal.
action: A bandwidth pass rather than a verdict on the deal - 'the team is focused on other opportunities at the moment' says their attention is committed elsewhere, not that anything here failed a screen. Nothing in the reply touches Houston, the submarket, the basis or the returns, so there is no objection to answer and nothing to re-cut. Notable only for what it is not: after a day in which Apollo named the submarket and Artisan named the micro-location, this one carries no market signal at all. Prieto answered off the 2 November follow-up with Sebastian Odriozola copied, warmly and with a close wish, so the relationship costs nothing to keep. Worth a note on the file for the next deal when their pipeline clears; worth nothing on this one.

quote: The opportunity is clearly laid out and the basis story is an interesting one. That said, single-asset US multifamily syndications sit outside how the families we work with build their real estate exposure, and a good part of the value here (depreciation, 1031) is designed for US taxpayers. action: The most useful pass of the week, and it is not about Houston at all. Krištofič names something no one else has said out loud: the two bullets the blast leads with - 'Depreciation' and 'Accept 1031 Exchange' - are worth nothing to an investor who does not file a US return. A Czech multi-family office reading that email sees two of the headline selling points as noise, and the hook that was added precisely to lift response rates is dead weight on the entire European wave. She also says single-asset syndications are not how her families take real estate exposure, which is a structural no on top of it. Read the two together and the conclusion is uncomfortable but cheap to act on: the European family-office sends need a different pitch - basis, occupancy, the dollar return - with the tax lines cut, or they should not go at all. Worth noting she read it properly before declining ('the basis story is an interesting one'), so the writing is landing; the targeting is what is off. New tag us-tax-benefit on this row.

title: Director
quote: At the moment, our investment activity is focused exclusively on direct value-add real estate investments in Spain, as well as on supporting and creating value within our existing portfolio companies. As such, we are not currently considering investments outside Spain or co-investment opportunities through third-party vehicles.

The send went to Pablo Serratosa Luján with two colleagues copied on 4 November and the reply came back from the Director two days later, which is a courteous firm answering properly rather than a screen - the relationship costs nothing to keep, and nothing about it suggests a future US deal would land either.

action: Courteous, immediate and empty of information. 'Focused on other strategies right now' is the shape a mandate answer takes when the reader does not want to explain the mandate, and there is nothing in it about Houston, the submarket, the basis or the check. Worth noting only as campaign evidence rather than deal evidence: it came back to zamir@myzmrcapital.com, which makes this the fourth GMass alias domain seen in two days alongside zmrcapitalgo.com, zmrcapitalstart.com and zmrcapitalmy.com. quote: Your Smart Living Allen Genoa deal came across my desk this morning. Buying a 2023 asset at $135K a door after the first buyer's capital stack broke is a good find, and the deck makes a clear case. Detailed Capital places LP and co-GP equity with family offices and institutional groups. Your $11.8M raise and Q1 close fit well with what our investors are looking for right now. Could we get 20 minutes next week to walk through the deal? | 10 Nov 21:15: "We are EST so in your time zone we look good for tomorrow Noon - 2 PT, Thursday 10-4 PT or Friday 10- Noon PT. Let me know what's best and we'll send invite out. Andy and I look forward to it."
action: The first genuinely INBOUND approach of the raise, and it is a broker rather than an investor. MacLennan is not offering money; Detailed Capital places LP and co-GP equity for a fee, so this is a third intermediary asking to sit between ZMR and the same pool of family offices. WHERE IT CAME FROM MATTERS. 'Came across my desk this morning' lines up with the GP-LP Match listing, which went live at 14:00 UTC today under a Premium membership. If that is the source, the paid platform's first result is an equity broker prospecting the listing rather than an LP reading it - worth knowing before judging whether the membership is working. BEFORE ANY CALL, TWO THINGS NEED CHECKING. First, the RJL engagement letter's non-circumvention runs to roughly 25 November and covers eleven named groups; a second placement agent working the same family-office universe is exactly the overlap that clause is written about. Second, Ackman-Ziff is already engaged and Brustein's live complaint is that the deal has been to nearly seventy LPs - adding a third party to the same list does not fix that and makes the story harder to control. The canonical equity list even keeps an 'Equity Broker' exclusion tab for firms in this category. None of which makes him wrong. He read the deck, he leads with the right fact (a 2023 build at $135K a door off a broken capital stack), and twenty minutes costs nothing. But the question to answer first is whether ZMR wants a third intermediary at all - not whether this one is any good. Note also he says 'Q1 close', which is a fourth version of the closing date now in circulation.  WINDOWS GIVEN, AND THEY DID THE WORK OF CONVERTING TO PACIFIC THEMSELVES. MacLennan came back inside an hour with three wide windows already translated out of Eastern, offered to send the invite, and confirmed Andy is joining. That is as easy as a counterparty gets. Pick one tonight. Tomorrow noon-2 PT is clear of both the 9:00 Eldridge call and whichever Dekel slot gets taken, so it is the cheapest of the three. THE INTERMEDIARY QUESTION STILL HAS TO BE SETTLED BEFORE THE CALL, not during it: RJL's non-circumvention runs to roughly 25 November and Ackman-Ziff is already engaged. Know what Zamir is willing to offer a third intermediary before Lyle and Andy ask.

followup.ask: Three windows offered (Wed noon-2 PT, Thu 10-4 PT, Fri 10-noon PT) and they will send the invite. Pick one tonight. Settle the intermediary question first - RJL non-circumvention to ~25 Nov, Ackman-Ziff engaged.

title: Director, Transactions Texas-West
quote: Zamir - My bad. Been an insanely busy two weeks for us. You free this afternoon after 130? We unfortunately have not been very active on multifamily lately but happy to discuss and see if there is interest internally.
action: TIME-SENSITIVE: he is offering a call TODAY. Nguyen sits in El Segundo, so 'after 130' almost certainly means 1:30 Pacific - about 21:30 UTC, roughly ninety minutes after this sweep. Nobody has answered yet, and this is the second time this week a same-day slot has been offered and left hanging; Oaktree's 12:30 only got confirmed at the last minute. Read the offer honestly though. 'We unfortunately have not been very active on multifamily lately but happy to discuss and see if there is interest internally' is a Director being candid that he has no mandate in hand and would be shopping it inside the firm, not a buyer leaning in. Against that: his title is Transactions Texas-West, which is exactly the desk this asset belongs to, and Emily Wickey and JP Perez are on the thread, so the right three people at a large insurance manager are reading it. The apology also tells you the silence since 30 October was workload, not disinterest - two chases (2 Nov, and yesterday's 07:31 call request) finally landed. Take the slot, lead with the Corebridge comp work (5.30-5.54% Houston trades against a 6.00% underwritten exit), and ask him directly what would have to be true for Manulife to look at a $11.77M LP position.

title: Director, Investments
quote: Zamir, can you please share the package and UW for this opportunity? Maybe we jump on a 30 minute intro call next week. Give me a few days/times that would work for you. | 10 Nov: "I was just called in for Jury duty tomorrow. Perhaps next week would be best. I'm flexible Monday and Tuesday after 9am pst."
action: The best reply of the day, and the only one that asks for more rather than less. Hollingsworth wants two things - the full package and the underwriting, and a 30-minute call next week with ZMR naming the times. Both are ours to send; nothing is pending on his side. The route it took is the point. The 4 November note went to Alexis Rains with Don Engle and a Carlton Senior Living address copied; Rains forwarded it internally to Hollingsworth at 19:44 on 5 November, and the Director of Investments wrote back the next evening. That is a family office circulating the deal to the person who actually underwrites - the opposite of the reflex passes that have filled this week. Note he asks for the UW specifically, not just the deck. That is the version question again: Kevin's Eldridge Acre package carried 20.9% deal-level / 2.27x with a 17.1% LP net, a 5.58% coupon and $11.73M, while the email Rains forwarded says 21.1% / 2.30x / 9.0% on 5.94% and $11.77M. Send him one set and be able to explain it; an investments director reading a model against the teaser that reached him will find the gap in ten minutes. Lead the call with the Corebridge comp evidence - closed same-vintage Houston trades at 5.30-5.54% against a 6.00% underwritten exit.  9 NOV - BOTH ITEMS SENT, AND A FOURTH NUMBER SET WENT WITH THEM. Zamir answered at 15:16 ('shoot around a few times that work for you this week') and asked Kevin to send the requested items; Kevin sent them at 20:42 with the full OM (ZMR_SmartLivingAllenGenoa_OM_11.26.pdf) and a model dated today (Houston_TX_SmartLivingAllenGenoa_ZMR_PF_11.09.26.xlsx). So the row flips: nothing is owed by us, and the call times are now Hollingsworth's to propose. He has the deepest document set of anyone on the board - OM plus live model, which not even Corebridge was sent. BUT READ WHAT KEVIN'S COVER NOTE SAYS, BECAUSE IT IS NOT THE CANONICAL SET. 'Updated to reflect our tax consultant's report and the recent movement in Treasuries': 21.1% deal-level IRR / 2.28x, with 17.2% / 1.97x shown as LP NET; 9.6% / 7.2% stabilized cash-on-cash on outstanding versus invested capital; a 6.00% TAX-ADJUSTED going-in cap, 6.00% exit, 7.00% untrended yield on cost; the agency coupon down to 5.51% from 5.71%; and $11.73M of LP equity rather than $11.77M. That is a fourth distinct set of headline numbers for the same asset in three weeks, after 20.3% (83 firms pre-27 Oct), 21.5% (the canonical re-underwrite and the blast) and 20.9% (Ackman-Ziff, brokered). It is also the FIRST TIME any recipient has been shown an LP-net return: everyone else has the deal-level figure. A reader who compares notes with another LP - and on a 170-firm distribution several will - finds four different IRRs and only one of them labelled. Two of the changes are substantive and in the right direction, which is worth saying plainly. The coupon fell because Treasuries moved, so the economics genuinely improved. And the occupancy claim was SOFTENED: 'two straight years at ~95% occupancy' became 'held occupancy in the low-to-mid 90s, peaking at 95-96% each spring and summer.' That is a more honest sentence and it is the version that survives a rent roll. The problem is that roughly 170 firms hold the stronger wording, including everyone still live. The comp distance also moved from 6.6 to 5.7 miles. ACTION: decide which set is now canonical and say so once, internally, before the next send. If 11.09 is the live model, the five unsent European redrafts, the CIM and every live row's follow-up all need to be reconciled to it - otherwise the next LP to ask 'which of these is right?' gets asked in front of a diligence team.  10 NOV 01:13 - HE CAME BACK WITHIN FOUR HOURS OF RECEIVING THE PACKAGE, WITH AVAILABILITY. Jury duty took tomorrow out, so he proposed next week instead: flexible Monday 16 and Tuesday 17 November after 9am PT. The row moves to a meeting and the ball is ours again - pick a slot and send the invite. The speed is the signal. Kevin sent the OM and the 11.09 model at 20:42; Hollingsworth replied at 01:13, which on Pacific time is the same evening. He did not ask a question or raise an objection, he moved straight to scheduling, and he kept Kevin, Chip and Mike Regan on the thread. Two things to settle before that call rather than during it. First, he is holding the 11.09 number set - 21.1% deal-level / 17.2% LP net, 5.51% coupon, $11.73M - which nobody else on the board has seen, so whoever runs the call needs to be working from that file and not the canonical 21.5% deck. Second, the occupancy line: KCB re-underwrote this deal to 93% off CoStar hours before this came in, and the OM Hollingsworth now holds carries the softened 'low-to-mid 90s' wording. If he asks why the model and the teaser differ, the honest answer is ready-made; if he does not ask, it is still better raised than discovered.

followup.ask: AVAILABILITY GIVEN: flexible Mon 16 and Tue 17 Nov after 9am PT (jury duty killed this week). Send an invite. He holds the 11.09 number set - run the call off that model, not the canonical deck.

quote: What is current average rents?
action: Four words, no greeting, no sign-off, sent on a Sunday - and it is the single most answerable question on the board. Ozur was the CC on the 30 October note to Jeff Garden; Garden never answered, the 2 November and 5 November chases went to him alone, and the CC is the one who finally wrote back. Exposure, full stop. This is what the page has been built around since October and it keeps being confirmed by the firms best placed to judge: Argosy ('tapped out on Houston right now, too much exposure'), LaSalle (chose a competing Houston deal), Barings ('Houston is not a target market'), and now Nuveen. FOUR SENDS TO GET IT: 30 October, 2 November, 5 November and 10 November. Goeke was the addressee every time, with Marc Roth, Carlos Burneo and Brian Wallick copied throughout, and he answered two and a half minutes after the fourth. Nothing to chase now, and the right time to go back is with something that is not in Houston.

title: Senior Managing Director
quote: Houston is not a market we have targeted for equity investment nor lending. There may be an exception for The Woodlands or Sugerland. Smart Living Allen Genoa is not located in an area we would have an interest. If you would like to catch-up we are available this afternoon.
action: THE MOST PRECISE HOUSTON ANSWER ON THE BOARD - IT NAMES THE LINE INSTEAD OF DRAWING IT. Nigro does not say Houston is closed; he says Houston is not targeted for equity OR lending, with a possible exception for THE WOODLANDS or SUGAR LAND, and then rules out this asset specifically: 'Smart Living Allen Genoa is not located in an area we would have an interest.' Those two exceptions are the affluent north and southwest suburbs. Allen Genoa is Southeast Houston, near the Ship Channel. So an investor who does both debt and equity has drawn the submarket line exactly where Slocumb, Sabal, Green Pine and Island Capital drew it on affordability and household income - and he drew it without being asked, having read only the bullets. That is the fifth independent read on the submarket rather than the market, and it is the one that names the acceptable alternatives. IT SHARPENS THE WHOLE 'HOUSTON IS CLOSED' FINDING. Nuveen, Barings and Argosy said the allocation is full. Nigro says something different and more useful: the capital exists for Houston, it is just not for this part of Houston. Read alongside LaSalle choosing a competing Houston deal, the pattern is less 'nobody wants Houston' and more 'the submarket is doing the work'. Worth reflecting in how the next memo frames the location. HE OFFERED A CALL THE SAME AFTERNOON and it is unanswered. Four sends (30 Oct, 2 Nov, 5 Nov, 10 Nov) produced a senior managing director volunteering time - take it, not to re-pitch Allen Genoa, which he has ruled out cleanly, but because he will tell you what he would fund in Houston and at what basis. That is worth more than another LP conversation.

followup.ask: Nigro offered a call "this afternoon" and it is unanswered. He passed on the deal but will do The Woodlands / Sugar Land, equity or debt. Take the call for the market read, not to re-pitch.

He asked for the deal terms 'between us' - meaning the split, not the OM - and whether the project can carry a loan and at what rate. Zamir sent the Strawman LP Terms document and, for the first time anywhere in this campaign, the full debt stack in writing: $23.8M at 70% LTV, 5.51% all-in, indexed to the 5-year Treasury at 4.62% as of 9 November, gross spread 1.35% less a 0.46% buydown for a 0.89% net spread, 60-month term, 24 months I/O, 30-year amortization, 3.19% closing costs. WHAT THIS ROW IS WORTH. An individual asking 'what rate would WE be looking at' is reading as a partner, not a screener, and he got term-sheet language within the hour. That is further than any institution on this board has been taken. It also means the terms are now in circulation and whatever is agreed here sets a precedent for the next LP who asks - worth knowing what is in that strawman before it travels further. He is reading the 11.10.26 numbers: 21.1% / 2.28x, 16.2% LP net, $12.03M ask.

followup.ask: Both questions answered within the hour and the Strawman LP Terms are with him. Ball is his - give it a day, then offer the call Zamir already proposed.
